Title: Kelantan couple struggle to afford sick son's special milk, resort to rice water
Article:
PASIR MAS: A couple in Kampung Kenjing, Repek, have seen their lives change drastically after their only child became bedridden four years ago due to brain damage caused by seizures.
Siti Noor Mastubaidura Ariffin, 36, said she had been running a small grocery business but was forced to close it to care for her 12-year-old son, Muhammad Aiman Mohamed, who requires constant attention.
"Since then, our family of three has depended on my husband, Rilhafizi Mohamad Zukhri, 44, who works as a labourer earning between RM50 and RM60 a day, depending on the jobs available.
"I prioritise spending his earnings on Muhammad Aiman's needs, including milk, disposable diapers and other care supplies.
"Sometimes, when we do not have enough money to buy his necessities, I have to put aside my pride and borrow money from my husband's employer and close relatives," she said when met at their rented home here.
The family was recently visited by the Social Welfare and Volunteer Club (KELSS), led by its Media and Communications Unit head Akidi Hamid, which provided cash assistance, disposable diapers and milk to help ease their financial burden.
Siti Noor Mastubaidura said Muhammad Aiman suffered four seizures within two months when he was eight, resulting in brain damage due to an infection.
"We spent two months at Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II), including a month in the intensive care unit, before Muhammad Aiman was allowed to return home," she said.
She said a box of specialised milk costing RM280 lasted only six days.
When money was particularly tight, she had to mix the specialised milk with regular milk and, at times, use rice water as a substitute.
"The RM500 monthly assistance from the Social Welfare Department is insufficient to cover Muhammad Aiman's needs, particularly his specialised milk, which costs at least RM1,200 a month.
"I use the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance to buy disposable diapers, which helps reduce our household expenses to some extent," she said.
She added that Muhammad Aiman required oxygen around the clock, forcing the family to rent an oxygen tank at a cost of RM7 a month.

Title: Two men held after car crashes into drain while fleeing police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two men suspected of stealing cables were arrested after the car they were travelling in crashed into a drain while fleeing from police in Taman Sri Watan, Ampang, yesterday.
Ampang Jaya police chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said police received a tip-off from the public at about 5.53am.
He said a police patrol spotted a blue Perodua Aruz without registration plates parked along Jalan Watan 8. The driver attempted to flee when police arrived, prompting a chase that ended when the car crashed into a drain.
"Both men in the vehicle were arrested," he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Sections 186, 379, 431A and 124K of the Penal Code, as well as Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Earlier, two videos showing police arresting the suspects behind a row of shops went viral on Threads. The videos also showed cables believed to have been targeted for theft.

Title: Trump says Putin 'would like to see a settlement' in Ukraine war
Article:
JOINT BASE ANDREWS: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin would like to reach a deal on the war in Ukraine, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of resisting a compromise.
"Russia would like to make a deal... but for whatever reason, Zelenskyy does not want to make a deal," Trump told reporters.
"President Putin would like to see a settlement, strongly," Trump said of what the Russian leader told him on Friday when the pair spoke on the phone.
Trump criticised the Ukrainian president for not holding an election since Russia first invaded Ukraine in 2022.
"I think he should have an election and he could have settled this thing many times," Trump said.
Trump and Zelenskyy traded barbs on Saturday after Washington moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.
Trump told reporters that Zelenskyy had disobeyed his orders not to strike Russian refineries and that the attacks risked worsening global fuel shortages caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Zelenskyy called Trump's diesel deal with Moscow a "weak decision".

Title: South Korea completes Arctic-Europe commercial voyage, eyes regular service despite risks
Article:
SEOUL, (South Korea): A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday, as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub.
The PanStar Acro docked in the southeastern port 50 days after setting sail on Aug 22.
Authorities say the Arctic route could cut typical voyage times by around a third.
President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030.
But the project risks friction with Western allies hoping to keep Russia isolated during its war in Ukraine.
The route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, and Seoul consulted with Moscow about the journey, including whether the ship needed ​help to tackle any problems, such as getting stuck in ice.
On its outbound voyage, the vessel passed through Arctic waters and reached its first European port, Felixstowe in Britain, before calling at Rotterdam and Gdansk and returning home via the Arctic.
The trial voyage also highlighted the challenges ahead. Before the departure, PanStar told Reuters it was seeking about 1,300 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo, but the ship left with 737 TEU of cargo plus empty containers.
Industry experts have said the route's value will depend on reliable schedules, the costs of slowing to avoid ice, special insurance premiums and extra fuel use. — REUTERS

Title: Jais probes allegations of a Muslim taking part in another religion's rituals
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) is investigating a viral social media post about an individual believed to be Muslim who allegedly took part in religious rituals of another faith that contravene Islamic law.
Director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said JAIS had launched the investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, which cover acts of worship carried out in violation of Islamic law and acts that bring Islam into disrepute.
"JAIS has so far been unable to confirm whether the individual carried out the act during the Thaipusam festival at Batu Caves, Selangor, as claimed in the viral post.
"We also cannot rule out the possibility that the post was altered using superimposition or artificial intelligence (AI)," he said in a statement today.
Mohd Shahzihan said JAIS is also investigating several aspects of the case, including where the incident took place, to determine whether the department has the jurisdiction to take further action under the applicable laws.
"JAIS takes issues concerning the faith of Muslims in Selangor seriously, and all information and complaints will be investigated in a professional, firm, timely, accurate and fair manner," he said.
The media reported yesterday that the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) and the authorities were taking action following the circulation of several video clips allegedly showing a Muslim individual participating in non-Muslim religious rituals.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said his department noted that the videos were also linked to alleged acts of worship and the use of certain incantations. — BERNAMA

Title: Bursa Malaysia seen trading within 1,600-1,630 points range next week with cautious upside bias
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia is expected to trade within the 1,600-1,630 points range next week, with a cautious upside bias on selective accumulation of blue chips.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said valuations were becoming more attractive, although fragile investor sentiment could temper buying interest.
"Looking ahead to next week, we expect selective bargain hunting to support a gradual recovery, although geopolitical uncertainties, elevated energy prices and volatile bond yields could limit the upside," he told Bernama.
For the trading week ended yesterday, Bursa Malaysia traded mostly higher supported by improved investor sentiment and ended the week higher, buoyed by market optimism and sustained buying activity following the 2027 Budget announcement, which provided fresh catalysts for the market.
Under 2027 Budget, the federal government has allocated a total of RM459.8 billion, up 3.6 per cent from the revised 2026 allocation, equivalent to 19.8 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Operating expenditure accounts for RM376.8 billion, while RM83 billion has been allocated for development expenditure (DE).
Education receives the largest allocation at almost RM69 billion, followed by health at RM47.7 billion and security with RM44 billion allocation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that Khazanah Nasional Bhd and InvestPenang will establish a RM100 million Strategic Investment Fund to support semiconductor and advanced manufacturing companies in their early stages of growth.
Meanwhile, IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said IPPFA Malaysia has forecast a GDP growth of 4.9 per cent in 2027, within the official range of 4.2 per cent-5.2 per cent.
"Sustaining this growth will depend on the strength of private consumption and investment, the fiscal multiplier of public spending, and the extent to which public investment crowds in private capital.
"The key policy challenge is to maximise domestic value added and growth multipliers while containing the fiscal deficit and preserving fiscal space," he said.
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) said investment growth in 2027 will be supported by higher DE of RM83 billion against RM81 billion in 2026, with major allocations directed towards transportation, education and training, healthcare, and trade and industry.
It said the construction sector should benefit from major infrastructure projects, including the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (E-ART) system, Kuala Lumpur Northern Dispersal Expressway (KL NODE), and Light Rail Transit Line 3 (LRT3) Phase 2.
RHB IB also said the services sector should remain a key growth contributor, supported by resilient private consumption, higher tourist arrivals following Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 and initiatives to accelerate digital-economy development.
"We remain broadly optimistic about manufacturing growth, underpinned by continued expansion in export-oriented industries, healthy investment spending and business-friendly policies.
"However, external uncertainties, including the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment cycle, geopolitical tensions and developments in United States tariff policy, could affect export demand and investment decisions.
"Malaysia's diversified economic base and supportive domestic policies should provide some buffer against these headwinds," it said.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 22.42 points to 1,608.45 at yesterday's close from 1,630.87 a week earlier.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index fell 71.74 points to 12,098.83, the FBM Top 100 Index lost 86.28 points to 11,871.40, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index added 69.46 points to 12,129.78.
The FBM ACE Index rose 125.11 points to 5,654.57, and the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 201.18 points to 17,683.11.
By sector, the Energy Index edged up 5.54 points to 838.57, the Plantation Index erased 166.29 points to 8,890.26, and the Industrial Products and Services Index climbed 2.23 points to 180.75. The Financial Services Index sank 615.69 points to 18,424.82.
Weekly turnover advanced to 19.63 billion units worth RM15.72 billion from 17.39 billion units worth RM14.42 billion in the previous week.
Main Market volume improved to 11.86 billion units valued at RM13.68 billion from 10.31 billion units valued at RM12.69 billion previously.
Warrants turnover strengthened to 4.91 billion units worth RM816.07 million from 4.40 billion units worth RM708.35 million in the previous week.
ACE Market volume expanded to 2.86 billion units valued at RM1.22 billion compared with 2.67 billion units valued at RM1.00 billion in the previous week.

Title: Ringgit expected to strengthen next week amid more cues from 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to strengthen against the US dollar next week, trading within the RM4.07 to RM4.08 range, as markets digest the 2027 Budget announcements for further cues on the country's economic outlook.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market attention would remain on 2027 Budget, with economists and analysts expected to examine the details and implications in the coming days.
"There are some measures, such as a tax cut for the M40 income group and more measures on the guarantees for SMEs via institutions such as Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) and Credit Guarantee Corporation (CGC). All these measures are meant to ensure that our businesses will remain vibrant," he told Bernama.
During the 2027 Budget tabled in the Dewan Rakyat, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed that the individual tax relief limit has been increased to RM12,000 from RM9,000, benefiting the middle-income group (M40).
Anwar also announced that Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) and Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) would provide up to RM32 billion in financing guarantees next year.
However, he said concerns over the external front, especially on interest rates in the US, will be among the key concerns for market players.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit eased against the greenback to 4.0830/0875 from 4.0820/0870 a week earlier.
The local currency traded mixed against a basket of other major currencies during the week.
It strengthened to 4.5807/5858 versus the euro from 4.5927/5983 on the previous Friday, and rose vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5791/5821 from 2.5906/5941. However, it depreciated against the British pound to 5.4063/4123 from 5.3927/3993 a week earlier.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.
It climbed versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1896/1934 from 3.1908/1952 a week earlier and inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.1/228.4 from 228.2/228.6.
The local note went up against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.52/6.54, but it depreciated vis-a-vis the Thai baht to 12.1735/1909 from 12.1579/1778 at the end of last week.

Title: FRIM, IIUM Braille book opens doors for visually impaired to explore endangered forest trees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The visually impaired can now learn about endangered forest tree species in Malaysia through a tactile and Braille book produced by the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) and the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM).
Titled
Sentuhan Rimba: Mengenali Biji Benih Spesies Hutan yang Terancam di Malaysia,
the book was developed under the Touch2Read project, combining tactile illustrations and Braille to help readers explore the physical characteristics of seeds and discover the diversity of the country's forest species.
FRIM director-general Datuk Dr Ismail Parlan said the initiative reflected efforts to make the country's forest heritage accessible to everyone, including the visually impaired.
"It is important to ensure that the visually impaired are not excluded from opportunities to learn about forest plant diversity, including identifying seed structures through touch," he said at the book's launch here yesterday.
FRIM supported the project by supplying actual seed samples to the IIUM Touch2Read team as references for developing the tactile illustrations.
The book features seven endangered forest tree species in Malaysia, with information on seed characteristics, botanical details and the uses of each tree.
Ismail said FRIM was ready to collaborate with various parties on similar initiatives to benefit the visually impaired.
[[nid:1552860]]
"We are willing and ready to continue this collaboration, perhaps through Touch2Read 3.0 or 4.0, to ensure FRIM can continue contributing to the visually impaired community," he said.
At the launch, visually impaired IIUM students also explored FRIM's Dipterocarp Arboretum through activities involving touching and smelling plants to learn about their natural characteristics.
Farhan Azkalwafa Sufyan, 25, who is pursuing a degree in Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL), said such activities helped visually impaired people identify and learn about plants through touch and hearing.
"We rely on our senses of hearing and touch. Touching tree trunks and leaves makes it easier for us to identify different types of trees in the forest," he said.
Commemorative posters were also presented to representatives of participating communities, agencies and strategic partners, including KL Braille Resources Sdn Bhd, Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Pendidikan Khas Setapak, the Malaysian Association for the Blind (MAB), the National Library of Malaysia and Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd. — BERNAMA

Title: Tax deductions for Food Bank donors to begin in 2027
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Special tax deductions for food and equipment donors under the Ihsan Food Bank Initiative (i-FB) will take effect from Jan 1, 2027, to Dec 31, 2030.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the incentive was aimed at encouraging wider participation from the corporate sector, voluntary organisations and other strategic partners in helping those in need.
He said the incentive was among 44 tax measures announced in the 2027 Budget following the acceptance of recommendations by the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry by the Prime Minister and Finance Ministry.
Armizan said the incentive would also recognise and encourage contributions of food, equipment and operational support to strengthen the implementation of i-FB.
"The tax incentive is in line with efforts to strengthen the food bank ecosystem through integrated coordination that creates wider opportunities for various parties to participate.
"The special tax deduction is one of the incentives and forms of recognition introduced to broaden the participation of strategic partners," he said.
He was speaking at the UMS Alumni Homecoming and Fundraising Dinner 2026 at a hotel here yesterday.
Armizan said details of the incentive's implementation mechanism would be coordinated with the Finance Ministry.
The i-FB is among the initiatives to address the cost of living through a nationwide approach involving government agencies, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and individuals.
Coordinated by the ministry's Cost of Living Division, the initiative is based on the 3S approach — Santuni Komuniti, Sayangi Alam and Selamatkan Makanan (Care for Communities, Love the Environment and Save Food).

Title: #NSTViral: Ministry officer rejects 'settlement' offer during cooking oil raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry enforcement officer has drawn praise online after rejecting an apparent attempt to negotiate an informal settlement during a raid on suspected hoarders of subsidised cooking oil.
In a video posted on TikTok by the ministry's Melaka branch under the username @kpdnmelaka, officers were seen inspecting a residential compound where blue plastic drums and boxes containing packets of cooking oil were stored.
When an individual attempted to negotiate an informal settlement, the lead officer immediately rejected the offer.
"Don't test me. If you want to talk somewhere else, I'll take you straight to MACC (Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission), nowhere else, just MACC," the officer warned.
When the storekeeper claimed that 25 cartons and drums of subsidised cooking oil were merely being kept temporarily at the premises, the officer challenged the explanation.
"You are the reason cooking oil disappears from the market. Retail shops are empty because everything is stashed here," the officer said.

Offering a bribe during an official inspection may also constitute an offence under Section 17(b) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years upon conviction.

Title: Execution survivor released from hospital, returns to prison
Article:
TENNESSEE, (United States): Death row inmate Christa Pike was released from a US hospital on Saturday and sent back to prison where she will continue receiving medical care following her botched execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said.
Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years, said attorneys Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen from Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee, and Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason from the Tennessee Office of the Post Conviction Defender in a joint release.
Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in the hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving the attempted execution on September 30, her lawyers said on Wednesday.
They previously believed she could be brain-dead.
Pike, 50, had been taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and ‌with severe arm injuries after two injections failed to kill her at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution.
A Tennessee judge this week ordered state officials to preserve all evidence related to their failed attempt to execute her, a development one of her lawyers called the "first of many steps to preserve and enforce her constitutional rights."
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look in to the botched execution of Pike and a similar failure involving Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous ​lines. — REUTERS

Title: Haze eases as Langkawi, Balik Pulau record healthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions showed significant improvement today, with Langkawi and Balik Pulau recording healthy air pollutant index (API) readings.
Langkawi, Kedah, recorded an API reading of 36, while Balik Pulau, Penang, registered 28.
This was an improvement from yesterday, when no locations nationwide recorded healthy API readings.
The Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal also reported a drop in the number of locations with unhealthy API readings to 19, from 33 yesterday.
Johor remained the state with the highest number of locations recording unhealthy readings, with Pasir Gudang at 183, Larkin (180), Tangkak (168), Kota Tinggi (167), Segamat (165), Pengerang (162), Kluang (160) and Batu Pahat (154).
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras and Batu Muda recorded API readings of 161 and 113, respectively, while Tasek Ipoh, Perak, registered 150.
In Pahang, Balok Baru and Rompin recorded readings of 158 and 156, respectively. In Terengganu, Kemaman registered 155, Kuala Terengganu (152) and Paka (104).
Bandaraya Melaka and Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded readings of 152 and 151, respectively.
Meanwhile, 47 locations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, including Indera Mahkota (99), Samalaju (98), Port Dickson and Miri (96), as well as Tanjung Malim and Seremban (95).
The APIMS portal reported no locations recording very unhealthy or hazardous API readings.

Title: Man dies after entering tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
Article:
LONDON: A man has died in a tiger attack after entering the animal's enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police said, PA Media and dpa reported.
Emergency services were contacted after the incident shortly after 1.30pm on Saturday.
Despite the efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.
His family have since been informed, South Yorkshire Police (SYP) said.
Videos circulating online appear to show a man being pawed at and grappled with by a tiger in an enclosure at the park.
The tiger was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident, while the wildlife park was subsequently evacuated, the force said.
A police spokesperson said: "At 1.35pm today, we received reports of a man entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injuries.
"Emergency services attended and, sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.
"The man's family are aware and are being supported by specialist officers. Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time.
"Regarding rumours surrounding the condition of the tiger, the animal was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident. There is no wider risk to the public."
A Yorkshire Ambulance Service spokesperson also confirmed that two land ambulances, the Yorkshire Air Ambulance and a doctor attended the scene.
A statement posted on the wildlife park's social media channels read: "We can confirm that a serious incident has occurred today at the tiger enclosure.
"Our emergency response procedures were immediately activated and emergency services are currently attending the scene.
"We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened.
"The safety and wellbeing of our visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority. The park is now closed and will remain closed tomorrow."
Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with the Land of the Tigers attraction opening in 2011.
The attraction is situated on a purpose-built, two-acre reserve for endangered Amur tigers, a subspecies with around 500 individuals remaining in the wild.
Photos of the enclosure on the park's website show a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the area where the tigers can roam.
South Yorkshire Police said they were aware of the footage circulating online and had asked people not to share it.

Title: Tanker catches fire after being struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz
Article:
ISTANBUL: A tanker caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Sunday, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The master of the outbound tanker reported that the vessel was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire on board, UKMTO said.
The crew were reported safe, while the extent of the damage and any environmental effects remained unknown.
Authorities are investigating, and vessels were advised to transit the area with caution.
The incident came hours after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said late on Saturday that an oil supertanker had struck a naval mine and exploded while attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorised southern route.
The IRGC said the vessel, which it described as capable of carrying around two million barrels of oil, had switched off its navigation systems before trying to cross the vital shipping route for global energy and commodity supplies.
It said the tanker struck a mine while trying to exit via the alternative route, triggering an explosion visible from coastal areas.

Title: Saudi-led coalition vows 'firm' response after 12 killed in attack on Riyadh airport
Article:
ISTANBUL: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen vowed early Sunday to respond "firmly" to an attack on the main airport in the capital Riyadh, which authorities said killed 12 people and injured 309 others, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki blamed the Houthis for the Saturday attack on King Khalid International Airport, saying it targeted one of the passenger terminals and killed and injured both travellers and airport workers.
Al-Maliki said the attack constituted a war crime under international humanitarian law and customary rules.
He said the coalition's Joint Forces Command would respond "firmly" and in line with international humanitarian law.
The Saudi civil aviation authority said early Sunday that the fatalities included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one citizen each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan.
The authority said 309 people were injured, including some in critical condition, and were getting treatment at hospitals.
The attack also caused material damage, which authorities said they were still assessing.
Operations at the airport were temporarily suspended on Saturday while officials assessed the damage and verified the safety of its facilities.
The attack came in the wake of recent Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and other facilities.

Title: IKEA Malaysia focusing on affordability and quality
Article:
BATU KAWAN: IKEA Malaysia is prioritising affordable, quality home furnishing and storage solutions under its financial year 2027 strategy, helping Malaysians maximise existing spaces without costly renovations.
Its country retail director Takeshi Murai said the focus on storage and organisation stemmed from extensive customer research and home visits, which revealed a strong desire among Malaysians to organise their belongings more effectively.
The strategy is anchored in IKEA's vision of creating a better everyday life for the many people, with affordability, functionality and quality remaining central to its approach.
"Low price and cheap are different. We want to be affordable. We want to be low price, which means we design our products and solutions with quality," Murai said.
At the core of IKEA Malaysia's philosophy is Democratic Design, a product development framework built on the belief that good home furnishing should be accessible to everyone, not just a privileged few.
Designed to balance form and function with affordability, the framework evaluates every product against five interconnected pillars: aesthetic design, practical functionality, everyday quality, sustainability for people and planet, and a low price point.
By integrating all five elements into every product — from simple storage boxes to complete wardrobe systems — IKEA ensures that lower prices do not come at the expense of durability or ethical production.
Rather than lowering retail prices by cutting manufacturing standards or using inferior materials, IKEA leverages its global supply chain, volume sales, and smart production processes to keep items budget-friendly.
Murai said this approach draws a clear line between being "cheap" and offering true value for money.
"By engineering efficiency directly into flat-pack packaging and material choices, products are built to withstand the rigors of daily life while remaining financially accessible to budget-conscious households facing rising cost-of-living pressures.
"In practical everyday living spaces, Democratic Design manifests in simple, thoughtful solutions tailored to real household habits," he added.
"Whether it is kitchen organisers that keep tools within reach, child-height entryway hooks, or display cabinets that protect sentimental family keepsakes while hiding daily clutter, each piece is designed to improve daily routines.
"We will never go for cheap. That's not who we are. We will go for low price, value for money. That's what we are."
Under the strategy, storage and organisation take centre stage as IKEA Malaysia seeks to help households make better use of the space they already have, rather than assuming they need bigger homes.
[[nid:1552796]]
The approach is brought to life through the message "A place for everything and everyone", reflecting the retailer's aim to provide practical solutions for different household needs, lifestyles and living arrangements.
Murai said the focus was informed by research, including IKEA Malaysia's first Home Organisation Index 2026, based on a nationwide survey of 506 Malaysians who make or share household purchasing decisions.
The index recorded an average home organisation score of 66 out of 100.
While only 9.5 per cent of respondents said they needed a bigger home, 85 per cent believed they could make better use of their existing space, and 37 per cent said they had sufficient storage but needed to organise it better.
"We have done hundreds of home visits and studied what customers really want in Malaysia. We discovered that many customers have a need and desire to improve how they organise their things at home," Murai said.
"We share the space, but we don't share the pace anymore."
Murai highlighted how IKEA's range caters to people living alone, families with children and multigenerational households.
He added that the retailer did not expect customers to embrace minimalism or discard belongings simply to achieve a more organised home.
Instead, IKEA aims to help Malaysians find practical ways to store the things they value, including sentimental keepsakes and personal collections.
Affordability remains another major pillar of IKEA Malaysia's financial year 2027 direction amid rising living costs, with the retailer reviewing its processes and supply chain to keep prices accessible.
Murai said IKEA was investing in lower prices across products that Malaysian customers valued, while maintaining quality, sustainability and responsible working conditions throughout its supply chain.
The retailer currently offers more than 1,200 products priced below RM10 and over 300
below RM5, with further price reductions on selected popular items.
Marking its 30th anniversary in Malaysia, IKEA also found that some of its popular products were cheaper today than they had been three decades ago.
Beyond pricing, the company is working to make its products and services more accessible through improvements to its online platform, customer pick-up services and online interior design offerings.
Murai said IKEA was also expanding its physical presence, with a store in Kuching scheduled to open in December, bringing the brand closer to customers in East Malaysia.
The affordability and storage priorities are being brought together through the Sorted Lah! campaign, which invites Malaysians to discover practical organisation ideas through interactive experiences at IKEA stores.
Weekend open houses will run from Oct 10 to Nov 1 at IKEA Damansara, Cheras, Tebrau and Batu Kawan, with activities designed to help visitors explore storage solutions and rethink how they use their homes.
One of the highlights is The Sorting Escape. Other experiences include The Design Table, The Listening Lounge and The Great Book Club, offering visitors ideas for tackling everyday clutter and making their homes work better.
Murai said the campaign reflected IKEA's belief that improving a home did not require major renovations or substantial spending.
He said small, affordable changes could make a meaningful difference to everyday living, reinforcing IKEA's commitment to helping Malaysians create functional, welcoming homes that suit their needs and budgets.

Title: Learn from India before Malayan tiger falls silent
Article:
THE recent
Economist Today
feature on India's wildlife success carries an uncomfortable message for Malaysia: a country can save its great animals, but only if it decides that protection is more than a policy statement.
India's growing encounters with tigers, leopards and elephants are often tragic.
Yet, as
The Economist
points out, they are also evidence of a striking conservation achievement;  wild animal populations have rebounded because the country chose to protect them at scale, over decades, through science, enforcement and political commitment.
Malaysia should pay close attention.
Our Malayan tiger is not merely another endangered species. It is the symbol on our coat of arms; a creature embedded in our national identity. Yet in the forest, it is slipping away.
From a population once believed to be in the thousands, estimates fell to fewer than 150 tigers in 2021, although recent reports suggest that conservation efforts may be yielding some improvement.
That is encouraging, but it is no cause for complacency.
A species does not recover because we celebrate small gains.
It recovers because we remove the threats that pushed it to the brink.
INDIA'S TIGERS THRIVE
India has demonstrated what sustained action can achieve. Through Project Tiger, launched in 1973, the country built a national system of protected tiger reserves, intensive patrolling, habitat conservation, scientific monitoring and stronger involvement of communities living near forests.
India's tiger population rose from an estimated 1,411 in 2006 to 2,967 in 2018, underlining what can happen when conservation is treated as a national mission rather than a periodic campaign.
The lesson is not that Malaysia should copy India blindly. India is far larger, with a different political structure, population density and wildlife landscape.
But the core principles are universal: protect habitat, stop poaching, restore prey, reconnect forests, involve communities and measure results honestly.
Malaysia has plans. We have the National Tiger Conservation Action Plan. We have the Central Forest Spine Master Plan.
We have dedicated officers, conservation groups, resear-chers, indigenous communities and corporate partners doing important work.
But the tiger does not need another beautifully printed strategy. It needs effective action in the places where it lives, hunts and dies.
A NETWORK OF PRIORITIES
The first priority must be uncompromising protection of tiger landscapes.
Tigers cannot survive in scattered forest fragments. They need large, connected landscapes with sufficient prey and safe routes through which they can move, breed and establish territories.
A wildlife corridor on paper means nothing if it has been cut by roads, plantations, mining, fencing or unplanned development.
Malaysia must therefore defend and restore the ecological links between key forests, especially across the Central Forest Spine.
Belum-Temengor, Taman Negara, Endau-Rompin and other critical landscapes should be treated as national ecological assets, not as vacant spaces awaiting the next development approval.
Infrastructure development must also change. Roads and railways that cut through wildlife habitat should include properly engineered crossings, fencing and monitoring systems.
Development and conservation need not be enemies — but development that permanently destroys wildlife movement routes is simply short-sighted planning.
The second priority is enforcement.
Poaching remains one of the gravest threats to the Malayan tiger. Snares are especially brutal: cheap, difficult to detect and indiscriminate.
They do not only kill tigers. They also trap deer, wild boar, tapirs, elephants and other animals that form the ecological web of the forest.
[[nid:1552793]]
Malaysia needs more rangers, better-equipped patrol teams, stronger intelligence gathering and closer coordination between the  Wildlife and National Parks Department, forestry departments, police, immigration, customs and border agencies.
Wildlife crime must be treated as serious organised crime, not as a minor environmental offence.
The third priority is prey.
A tiger cannot survive in a forest emptied of deer and wild boar. When poachers remove prey species, they weaken the entire food chain.
Tiger recovery must  include aggressive action against illegal hunting, regular monitoring of prey numbers and habitat management that supports the full ecosystem, not just the tiger as a national icon.
COLLECTIVE EFFORT CRUCIAL
India's experience is instructive here.
Its tiger monitoring goes beyond counting the big cats.
It considers prey, forest quality, human pressure and habitat connectivity. That is the level of seriousness Malaysia must embrace.
But conservation cannot be enforced solely from Putrajaya or state capitals. The people who live nearest to the forest must be central partners.
Orang Asli communities, villagers, plantation workers and smallholders often bear the risks of living alongside wildlife.
If they lose livestock, crops or income, they deserve speedy and fair compensation.
They should also benefit from conservation through paid ranger support, restoration work, eco-tourism, monitoring programmes and community-based enterprises.
India's conservation model increasingly recognises that communities and wildlife must coexist, even though this remains difficult and imperfect.
Malaysia must pursue the same principle with greater empathy and respect for local rights, knowledge and livelihoods.
Saving the Malayan tiger is  a test of national seriousness.
We cannot keep praising the tiger as a national emblem while allowing its habitat to be fragmented, its prey depleted and its survival left to under-resourced enforcement teams and civil society groups.
The tiger's fate will reveal whether Malaysia is prepared to protect its natural heritage with the same urgency it brings to roads, industries and economic growth.
India proves that recovery is possible.
Malaysia has the forests, the expertise and the public goodwill. What we need now is political courage, sustained funding and a whole-of-nation commitment.
The Malayan tiger should not become a symbol that survives only on our crest, in our stories and in our memories.

Title: 'Throw the book' at lorry firms over road accidents, experts say [WATCH]
Article:
fuadnizam@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities should throw the book at lorry companies for road accidents involving their drivers, a road safety activist and a criminologist said.
This, they said, was necessary after repeated calls by the authorities for enhanced safety on the roads had been ignored.
The employers must face legal consequences for negligence and failure to enforce safety measures, they added.
Their call came after a 10-tonne lorry rammed into 11 vehicles at a traffic-light junction in Alam Budiman, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Shah Alam on Friday.
Four people were injured in the incident.
The 51-year-old lorry driver was arrested after a urine test returned positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
Road safety activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said such incidents have occurred repeatedly despite warnings from authorities, including the transport minister, with dangerous driving, driving under the influence  and vehicle overloading continuing to endanger lives.
"Employers should not be allowed to shift the blame entirely to drivers whenever accidents occur," he said.
"Morally, I would say the employers have a responsibility.
"When they employ drivers, first and foremost they must make sure that these drivers are disciplined, responsible and have enough rest when they drive."
Lee also raised concerns over payment arrangements based on the number of trips completed, saying such incentives could encourage drivers to work longer hours at the expense of road safety.
He called for stricter limits on commercial drivers' working hours, similar to those imposed on pilots, as well as a review of existing laws and stronger enforcement against drivers and employers who disregard safety requirements.
Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said the country already had substantial penalties for drug-impaired driving under Section 44 of the Road Transport Act, particularly for offences resulting in injury or death.
However, he said the Shah Alam incident raised questions about whether existing laws were being enforced consistently enough to prevent foreseeable harm.
"From a criminological perspective, deterrence depends not merely on the severity of punishment, but also on the certainty, and swiftness of detection and enforcement.
"Authorities should consider tougher consequences for repeat offenders, including appropriate licence suspension or disqualification, alongside targeted drug screening and effective prosecution," he said.
"Preliminary positive screening results, however, must be followed by proper investigation and due process."
Sundramoorthy said transport operators should conduct fitness-to-drive checks, maintain documented vehicle inspections, verify commercial driving licences and establish procedures for reporting suspected impairment.
"Where evidence establishes negligence or deliberate disregard of safety obligations, companies and responsible managers should face proportionate legal consequences.
"However, corporate liability should be based on evidence rather than imposed automatically whenever an employee commits an offence."
He said there should be better coordination among enforcement agencies and transport operators, with targeted road operations, risk-based drug screening and accident data used to identify recurring risks.
To address wider weaknesses in the criminal justice system, Sundramoorthy proposed establishing a Criminal Justice Advisory Committee comprising criminologists, legal experts and enforcement agencies to assess the effectiveness of existing laws and recommend evidence-based reforms.
"The real test of criminal justice policy is not how severely we punish after an incident, but how effectively we prevent the next one," he added.

Title: 2027 Budget: Elderly care plans face execution test
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Caring for ageing parents while raising children of their own places a double burden on some families, as medical bills, professional care and daily expenses will stretch household budgets.
Therefore, the 2027 Budget  has raised hopes of greater support, but elderly care service providers  and senior citizens say effective implementation will be key to easing the strain.
National Secretary of the Association of Residential Aged Care Operators of Malaysia (Agecope) Fong Muntoh described the 2027 Budget as a long-awaited breakthrough  after 27 years in the business.
"This is the first time I have seen a budget bring together so many meaningful measures for seniors and the families supporting them.
"The government has taken a very positive step."
Fong said the allocation of more than RM40 million to train 8,000 people for the elderly care sector could help address the shortage of caregivers.
He also cited the reduction in service tax from 8 per cent to 6 per cent and the exemption for elderly care fees of up to RM96,000 a year as measures that could ease the financial burden on families.
The planned National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence in Penang and Sarawak, which were expected to support training, research and elderly care, were another encouraging development, he said.
[[nid:1552723]]
Fong added that  the measures could also ease the pressure on the "sandwich generation", whose members must care for ageing parents while supporting their own families.
"Now we await the implementation. The announcements are good. Let us hope the delivery is just as good," he said.
Senior care activist Tony Lian, who runs several charitable  care centres, said elderly care should be a shared responsibility rather than a burden borne  by individuals and their families.
He said the RM1.3 billion allocation for
Bantuan Warga Emas,
tax relief for family caregivers and investment in care facilities and training reflected greater recognition of the needs of the elderly.
"These measures recognise that ageing is not just an individual or family responsibility, but a shared responsibility that requires government and community support.
"We are an ageing nation. A dignified old age should be a right, not a privilege.
"The 2027 Budget helps make  that a reality," he said.
Lian, however, hopes more can be done to help poor, homeless elderly people found abandoned on the streets and in hospitals.
For 65-year-old Nur Mastura Mohd Khalid, the proposed monthly withdrawal option for Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings could help retirees manage their finances and budget for daily necessities, medical bills and other  expenses.
She also said the reduction in service tax on elderly care services could ease the burden on primary caregivers and families paying for professional care.
However, she said that the measures must provide meaningful relief to retirees and families facing a burden who had to grapple with increased costs.
Beyond financial assistance,  C.K. Leong, 67, called for safer and more accessible public facilities to help  the elderly  remain active and independent.
She said elderly-friendly facilities should be available in every neighbourhood —  including safer walkways, accessible parks  with elderly-friendly exercise machines and affordable day-care centres — particularly for low-income households.
[[nid:1552722]]
Leong said poorly designed pavements and high kerbs could discourage older people from walking and exercising.
She  proposed installing lifts in older walk-up apartment blocks, with the government and apartment owners sharing the costs.
She said   owners should be allowed to use their EPF savings to cover part of their contribution, subject to approval.
Meanwhile, P. Inahsav, 57, said  private-sector retirees risked being overlooked despite efforts to strengthen support for senior citizens.
She suggested the  proposed minimum monthly pension of RM1,350 as a positive move, but questioned whether it would cover daily necessities and healthcare, particularly for elderly people without family support.
Inahsav said retirees without government pensions could face  financial pressure as  the cost of living and medical expenses continued to rise.
She called for the private-sector retirement age to be raised to 65, allowing healthy people with insufficient savings to continue working and build their retirement funds.
"Covid-19 took a hit on most people's savings, EPF and livelihood.
"If politicians can work until their 70s or 80s, why can't ordinary citizens who are struggling to make ends meet continue working until 65, especially when they are  healthy and able?"
She added that those financially prepared for retirement should retain the option to retire earlier, while others should have the opportunity to work longer.
[[nid:1552721]]

Title: Haze: Malaysian, Singaporean firms under investigation
Article:
JOHOR BARU: JOHOR BARU:  A Malaysian plantation group and several Singapore-linked companies have been linked to Indonesian concessions where fire hotspots were detected.
Indonesian authorities have not disclosed the identities or nationalities of the 19 companies investigated over fires that burned 11,047ha across seven provinces.
A report by Greenpeace Indonesia, Greenpeace Malaysia and Pantau Gambut identified at least one Malaysian company alongside four concessions linked to Singapore-based companies.
The findings, released on Oct 5, however, did not directly blame them for starting the fires in Sumatra and West Kalimantan, or committing any offence.
Indonesian Consul-General in Johor Baru Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto said they  identified 57 businesses across eight provinces in their enforcement crackdown.
Indonesia's Environment Ministry had linked the businesses to open burning covering 33,514ha.
Authorities recorded 97 police reports involving corporations and were investigating 46 suspects, including five companies.
The Forestry Ministry imposed administrative sanctions on 26 companies, including revoking five permits, suspending 13 and issuing written warnings or restoration orders to eight.
On Thursday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto had agreed to address the worsening haze, as Malaysia renewed calls for stronger regional cooperation.
Meanwhile, Sari Wilson-Pohan, an Indonesian who has lived in Johor since 2014, said she was embarrassed and saddened by what she viewed as a lack of urgency by Indonesia in addressing the fires. Both her sons attend school in Johor and her husband works in Singapore.
"Regardless of who owns the companies, Indonesia must put humanity first. Protecting people, the environment and our future should always come before protecting big businesses," she told the
New Straits Times.
She said  she had   submitted an open letter to Prabowo urging decisive action and accountability.
"Enough is enough. People must come before profits."

Title: 2027 Budget: Budi Belia 'a good starting point'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For young Malaysians who give their time to help others, RM100  may cover the cost of getting to a volunteering session, but the satisfaction of making a difference is what keeps them going.
The proposed Budi Belia e-wallet incentive under the 2027 Budget could draw more youths into community work, particularly students who struggle to meet expenses, but those already volunteering say sustaining their interest will take more than financial rewards.
Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) veterinary student Yaashinii Naaidu Sri Sivabalasundram, 22, who volunteers at the Furry Kids Safe Haven dog shelter in Rantau, Negri Sembilan, said the money could help cover transport, meals and other expenses.
"Although it may not be a huge amount, it can serve as a good starting point to encourage youth participation," she said.
But Yaashinii said she would continue volunteering even without the incentive because of her commitment to animal welfare.
"I would have volunteered anyway because I genuinely care about animal welfare and enjoy contributing to a meaningful cause," she said.
[[nid:1552695]]
For Nor Arisha Natasha Mustapar, 25, the incentive could help youths take their first step into volunteering, even if money was initially their main motivation.
The UPM graduate, who works at Sanofi-Aventis (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, has joined initiatives including delivering aid to B40 households through Yayasan Belia Malaysia's Harapan Ramadan 2026 programme, serving food with Feeding the Needy in Chow Kit and teaching underprivileged students through Tuisyen Madani.
"I see it less as a payment for their service and more as a small incentive to encourage them to take their first step," she said, adding that the experience could help them develop empathy and a stronger sense of social responsibility.
For Nor Syazlin Ishak, 22, who has volunteered with Feeding the Needy, BeKind Malaysia and Special Kids Therapy Centre, the value of volunteering lies in the human connection it creates.
"It is not only about providing food but also about making people feel valued, respected and cared for," she said, adding that simple gestures, such as wishing someone a good night or asking them to take care, could make a difference.
However, Nur Durrah Annisa Rusidi, 23, said getting young people involved was only half the challenge, as keeping them engaged required meaningful opportunities to contribute.
[[nid:1552694]]
"We need to make volunteering meaningful, not just financially attractive," she said.
Durrah, who previously volunteered through her university's organisation, Majlis Mahasiswa Anak Perlis, is working towards establishing a non-governmental organisation, GenzPerlis.
She said young people should be trusted with greater responsibility, including leading projects and participating in decision-making.
"Give us the platform, let us lead projects, involve us in decision-making and take our voices seriously.
The volunteers called for Budi Belia to support a wider range of causes, including animal welfare, environmental conservation and community service, while creating more opportunities for sustained involvement rather than one-off activities.
Yaashinii said this would allow youths to build lasting connections with the causes they support.
Meanwhile, Durrah said "the real success of Budi Belia would be when young people continue showing up, even after the incentive is gone".
Syazlin, who developed an interest in volunteering while in secondary school, said the experience had broadened her perspective and taught her to be more compassionate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Traumatised Panamanians begin quake recovery
Article:
CHITRE: Residents near the epicentre of a major earthquake in southern Panama began cleaning up on Saturday, traumatised by the previous day's heavy shaking that left widespread damage but, so far, no reported deaths.
"This is something we've never seen before. We weren't prepared for this kind of event," said Aldulfo Quintero as he cleared debris from a store in Chitre, about 250km southwest of Panama City.
The 41-year-old told AFP he had a "great fear" that a new earthquake could strike at any moment.
After the initial 7.7-magnitude quake around midday on Friday, more than 100 aftershocks had been recorded, some as strong as magnitude 6.0.
Like many others in Chitre, the capital of hard-hit Herrera province, 28-year-old Yakshuri Castillo chose to sleep outdoors due to fears of another quake.
She told AFP she "went into shock" when the first quake struck.
Dozens of homes were damaged in the city, whose 66,000 residents were still without electricity on Saturday.
The epicentre of the initial quake was recorded by the US Geological Survey (USGS) about 60 kilometres away, near the border of Herrera, Los Santos and Veraguas provinces.
Earthquakes are rare in Panama and usually occur in western Chiriqui province, bordering Costa Rica.
Strong shaking in Panama City, more than 200km from the epicentre, sent panicked people pouring into the streets from the capital's numerous high-rise buildings.
[[nid:1552842]]
While no deaths have been reported from the quake, about 30 people have been treated for minor injuries.
Authorities are still assessing the damage in remote areas. Several communities have been cut off due to roads damaged by the quake.
"The disaster we are facing is massive," President Jose Raul Mulino said upon arriving in one of the affected areas.
The United States, which counts Panama among the members of President Donald Trump's new "Shield of the Americas" initiative, has pledged rapid support.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on X on Friday that he was "closely monitoring" the situation, with his office "rapidly mobilising resources and personnel to assist".
The top US military commander in the region, Francis Donovan, has "directed immediate support to help the people of Panama, including on-the-ground support from rotary-wing aircraft... and the airlift of key personnel and supplies into the country", US Southern Command said in a statement on Saturday.
The Panamanian quake is at least the fourth earthquake this year in Latin America to surpass magnitude 7.0, following devastating back-to-back earthquakes in Venezuela's Guaira in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins top photography prize at Bayeux
Article:
BAYEUX: Palestinian freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda on Saturday won the photography category at the prestigious Bayeux award for war correspondents for his work from Gaza.
The Washington Post, NPR (National Public Radio, US) and CNN won the top prizes in the print, radio and television categories for reports from Ukraine, Gaza and the West Bank respectively.
As well as the top prize, Hamda, who is based in the Gaza Strip, also won the Public's Choice award for his reportage "What War Leaves Behind".
He was not at the ceremony in Bayeux, northwest France, but sent a video message to the event.
"My greatest honour is that these photos have been able to leave the borders of Gaza," he said.
Hamda submitted his unpublished reportage to the Bayeux jury himself. It illustrates life in the Gaza Strip and the hardship its inhabitants are enduring after Israel launched its offensive there following Hamas's Oct 7 attack three years ago.
The Washington Post team was honoured for telling the story of a Ukrainian soldier trapped in a combat zone for 177 days.
Palestinian journalist Anas Baba of NPR won the radio award for a report on the recovery of victims' bodies in Gaza.
CNN journalists won both the television prize and video image award for their report on Israeli soldiers serving settlers in the West Bank.
Associated Press photographer Jehad Alshrafi took the Young Reporter photography prize for his series "Endless War and Devastation in Gaza".
One of Alshrafi's photos, showing footballers playing on a pitch surrounded by rubble in Gaza, sparked controversy in France in August.
It was removed from a sports photography festival in the northern French town of Deauville before a court ordered it reinstated.
Veteran BBC war correspondent Lyse Doucet was president of the Bayeux awards jury.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Power restored in eastern Cuba after outage
Article:
HAVANA: Power was restored in eastern Cuba on Saturday, several hours after an outage caused by a partial grid failure, the national power company said, as the island reels from a months-long US oil blockade.
"The partial disconnection of the national grid in the eastern region is over," Union Electrica de Cuba (UNE) said.
Nearly three hours earlier, the company said a failure on the line linking Nuevitas to Tunas province had sparked an outage, without specifying how many provinces were affected.
Cuba, a nation of 9.4 million people, has suffered repeated power outages, and rolling blackouts can last up to 20 hours a day. These outages also affect water supplies and telephone services.
The problems are due in part to ageing energy infrastructure, with power plants falling into disrepair and requiring weeks of maintenance.
Since January, the United States has effectively cut off the oil supply to Cuba as part of a multi-faceted pressure campaign, complicating the delivery of fuel needed to keep backup generators running.
Cuba has experienced seven nationwide blackouts since the start of the year, and a dozen since late 2024.
UNE says fuel shortages make the network more vulnerable to outages.
Two years ago, the government launched a major programme to install solar panels with China's backing. According to official data, renewable sources account for 21 per cent of Cuba's energy mix.
Relations between the United States and Cuba have been tense since the start of 2026, when US forces captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, a major ally of Havana.
The administration of US President Donald Trump has asserted that Cuba, located 150km off the coast of Florida, poses an "extraordinary threat" to US national security and has not ruled out military intervention to prompt economic and political reforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron popularity lowest since taking office
Article:
PARIS: French President Emmanuel Macron's popularity has fallen to its lowest level since taking office in 2017, according to a poll published on Saturday.
The Ipsos BVA-Cesi survey found that just 15 per cent of respondents held a favourable view of Macron, down one point from a month earlier and the lowest score of his presidency.
The poll comes as France faces record fuel prices and protests by high school students, with respondents citing purchasing power as their top concern.
Worries about the future of the country's welfare system and France's debt levels also ranked highly.
Among politicians seen as potential successors to Macron, far-right leaders Jordan Bardella and Marine Le Pen remained the most popular, with approval ratings of 33 and 32 per cent respectively.
Both lost ground from a month ago, with Bardella losing three points and Le Pen four, after a report accused Bardella of having written antisemitic messages in his youth from an old Facebook account.
Commissioned by La Tribune Dimanche newspaper, the online poll was conducted on September 7-8 among 1,000 adults and had a margin of error of between 0.6 and 3.1 percentage points.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil's Lula accuses Meta of election interference
Article:
BRASILIA: The campaign of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva accused tech giant Meta of election interference on Saturday after his social media content was allegedly blocked on the company's platforms.
The leftist leader is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in the October 25 runoff, where he will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.
In a statement, Lula's campaign reported instances where platforms owned by Meta — the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram — allegedly restricted the distribution of his content.
The campaign claimed that in recent days, Meta "prevented President Lula's profile from promoting Instagram feed posts", while a post from his official account "experienced an interruption in view counts, which affected its reach".
It also said that prior to last Sunday's first round of voting — in which Flavio Bolsonaro finished first — the profiles of Lula and other leftist leaders "suddenly disappeared from Instagram's search function".
"The series of technical issues... raises strong suspicions that Meta's actions constitute an attempt to interfere in the Brazilian electoral process to the benefit of Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy," the statement added.
Meta's Brazil office denied the charges, calling them "simply false" and "not supported by the facts".
"Many of the technical issues mentioned did not affect only Brazil or specific accounts," Meta told AFP in an email.
"We comply with electoral regulations and are committed to a level playing field regarding the use of our platforms."
Lula's campaign has filed a complaint with the electoral court over the alleged social media blocks.
Following the first round of voting, Lula — who does not use a mobile phone — launched a social media push that includes videos of him addressing his online followers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Attack on Saudi airport leaves 12 dead, dozens wounded
Article:
RIYADH: The third attack this week on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday left at least 12 people dead and more than 300 wounded, Saudi authorities said, and the Iran-backed Houthis claimed responsibility for the strike, a major escalation of their campaign against the Saudis.
The dead included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
Hospitals were flooded with wounded people brought by ambulance and helicopter, people briefed on the matter said. Some were in critical condition.
Saturday's attack occurred without warning, with no alert issued by Saudi Arabia's threat warning system. This week's two previous attacks on King Khalid International Airport left four people dead and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.
This week's deadly strikes exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom's self-defence capabilities as it waged an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the Iran-backed group.
Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes on targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed civilians, including women and children.
Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
All flights were diverted from Riyadh on Saturday, and operations at the airport, which serves a city of roughly 8 million people, were temporarily suspended, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
The head of the Houthi media office said in a post on X after the attack that the group had "shut down Riyadh international airport". The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group on Monday.
US President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether Washington planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.
"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he said.
Eyewitness saw wounded on the ground
One eyewitness at the airport on Saturday reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility. A video verified by Reuters showed ambulances at the airport.
An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.
The US embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas".
Saudi Arabia entered the Yemen war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to force the Houthis out of the Yemeni capital, Sanaa. The Houthis had stormed Sanaa the previous year, pushing out government forces.
The war was fought to a bloody stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine. Saudi Arabia struck a 2022 deal with the Houthis, freezing the conflict.
That ceasefire unravelled over the summer, culminating in a lightning Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces.
The Saudi-backed Yemeni government began an offensive this week to try to retake that territory, which has so far made slow gains, even as the Houthis put the country's third-largest city, Taiz, under siege.
Riyadh due to hold major summits
Flight-tracking site Flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.
Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host major energy and investment conferences.
Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and sought to reassure attendees about their security.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nine people, including children, dead after mass shooting in Pennsylvania
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: A 45-year-old man shot and killed eight people in Erie, Pennsylvania, including a pregnant woman and two children, then apparently shot himself dead, authorities said on Saturday at a press conference where they revealed details of the previous evening's shooting.
The shooter, who has yet to be identified, died of an apparent self-inflicted wound before officers arrived at the scene, said Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah.
"Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said.
Police have yet to establish a motive, Lorah said. He said eight of the nine who died in the shooting were family members, and one was a family friend.
Lorah said that after the shooter entered the home, he came out of the house and shot two women who appeared "distressed" and were pacing back and forth seeking assistance from neighbours.
Police found the suspect on the second floor of the home on Perry Street, Lorah said.
Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said the police department "arrived at a horrific scene, faced unimaginable circumstances, and carried out their duties with courage and professionalism".
"They too are members of this community, and they too will carry the weight of what happened last night," she said.
Earlier, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said in a statement on X that he had spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered support following "the tragic mass shooting".
Shapiro has long advocated for "common sense gun safety" and pushed the Pennsylvania General Assembly in 2024 to pass gun reforms, including universal background checks and restrictions on ghost guns, which are homemade guns that lack serial numbers and cannot be traced. Several of Shapiro's proposals have stalled in the state legislature.
There have been more than 400 mass shootings in the US in 2026, according to data compiled by Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as one in which four or more people are shot, excluding the shooter.
The last recorded mass shootings in Pennsylvania took place in July in Philadelphia, according to the data.

Title: Evacuations, injuries at Riyadh airport after alleged Houthi attack
Article:
RIYADH, Saudi Arabia: Yemen's Houthis attacked Riyadh's international airport with a missile on Saturday, a diplomatic source told AFP, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal.
Saudi authorities did not confirm any new attack or evacuation, but one witness reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.
"I was on gate 403" at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP.
"I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running."
A source at a local hospital told AFP that five people were in intensive care after being wounded at the airport, saying "dozens of people were injured" in all.
The relative of one injured person said they had been wounded in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass, and had been taken to hospital.
Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport.
"Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target," the diplomatic source told AFP, saying the airport was hit by "a missile around 3pm" (1200 GMT).
The airport was hit by deadly attacks claimed by Yemen's Houthis on Thursday, though the Iran-backed group did not announce any fresh strikes on the facility on Saturday.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen's Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.
Admissions by Saudi authorities of strikes hitting civilian targets are relatively rare, with officials issuing few statements on Houthi attacks in recent weeks.
The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war that has spread across the Middle East.
Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen's government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour's civil war.
Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalling a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy.
'CONTACT YOUR AIRLINE'
Earlier on Saturday, Riyadh airport urged passengers to check their flight status before coming – echoing an advisory sent on Thursday, when attacks killed three people including a pilot for Saudia, the national airline.
"Please contact your airline directly and confirm your flight status before heading to the airport," read a statement posted on the airport's official X account on Saturday.
Thursday's Houthi-claimed attacks also badly damaged a grounded Saudia plane.
Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP.
The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country's entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.
The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area – a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping – but they claimed to have repelled the assault.
Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
