Title: Budget 2027: Tax breaks to encourage corporate support for food bank initiative, says Armizan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — A special tax deduction incentive for the Ihsan Food Bank Initiative (i-FB) under Budget 2027 is expected to encourage greater participation by strategic partners, including the corporate sector, in strengthening the food bank ecosystem.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the government had agreed to grant special tax deductions to parties contributing food and equipment for the i-FB initiative from January 1 next year until December 31, 2030.
He said his ministry appreciated Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Finance Ministry for accepting its proposal to support the implementation of i-FB, one of 44 tax incentive measures announced under Budget 2027.
“This tax incentive is in line with efforts to strengthen the food bank ecosystem through integrated coordination that opens the door as widely as possible to participation by various parties,” he told a press conference before attending the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Alumni Homecoming & Fundraising Dinner 2026, last night.
According to him, the special tax deduction introduced serves as an incentive and recognition to broaden the participation of strategic partners, including through contributions of food, equipment and operational support needed to strengthen the implementation of i-FB.
Armizan said the detailed mechanism for implementing the special tax deduction incentive for i-FB would be coordinated with the Finance Ministry.
He added that collaboration with strategic partners, including the corporate sector and voluntary organisations, would enable i-FB to drive collective efforts to ease the cost-of-living burden on those in need, rescue food from waste and protect the environment.
Meanwhile, at the dinner, i-FB grants were also presented to the UMS Student Consumer Movement, which will coordinate the initiative at their respective educational institutions and within local communities.
Armizan said the initial grants would be used to provide equipment and dedicated i-FB spaces on campuses to facilitate the receipt, storage and distribution of donated food to students in need.
“This initiative also creates opportunities for contributions from various parties to help ease the cost of living among students,” he said.
The i-FB initiative is one of the cost-of-living assistance measures implemented nationwide, with the Cost of Living Division of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living serving as its secretariat and aiming to secure participation from government agencies, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and individuals. — Bernama

Title: CM: Penang ready to work with Putrajaya on new elderly care, research centre
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 11 — Penang is ready to work with the federal government to establish the National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) in the state as part of efforts to prepare for an ageing population.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would cooperate in implementing the initiative, announced in Budget 2027 yesterday, which aims to provide training, research and care facilities for the elderly.
He said the State Economic Planning Division (BPEN) would be asked to liaise with the relevant ministries to obtain details of the proposed development, as information on its location and implementation in Penang was not yet available.
“We certainly welcome it and the state government will provide cooperation to ensure this facility can be established in Penang,” he told reporters after officiating the second State Heritage Declaration Ceremony under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011 for 2026 here yesterday.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced when tabling Budget 2027 yesterday that two NICE facilities would be developed in Penang and Sarawak to provide training, research and elderly care as the country prepares for an ageing population.
Chow said the growing number of senior citizens required targeted policies and programmes to ensure their welfare and needs were addressed effectively.
He said Penang was expected to become an ageing state in the next few years, adding that addressing the associated challenges required not only government action but also the involvement of the private sector and the community.
“The state government, the private sector and the community must all take the ageing process and the status of an ageing state seriously. This requires policies, infrastructure, care homes for the elderly, awareness programmes, welfare support and so on,” he said.
In a separate development, Chow said the state government would seek further information on the proposed 122-acre NCT InnoSphere development involving Penang and Kulim, Kedah, which was also announced in Budget 2027.
Anwar said NCT InnoSphere would be developed as a heavy vehicle, engineering, maintenance and logistics hub to support industries in Kulim and Penang under efforts to further strengthen the Special Border Economic Zone (SBEZ). — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM1.1b for enforcement agencies signals stronger anti-corruption push, says MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The RM1.1 billion allocation to enhance the operational capabilities of law enforcement agencies, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), reflects the government’s strong commitment to combating crime, including corruption, and strengthening national governance.
In a statement yesterday, the MACC described this as evidence of the government’s recognition of the importance of empowering enforcement agencies to prevent and eradicate crime, bring criminals to justice, and recover assets for the nation.
According to the MACC, the government’s emphasis on drafting the Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten the governance of entities entrusted with managing public funds and assets reflects a commitment that goes beyond merely combating abuse of power to actively strengthening governance.
“This step is seen as capable of preventing major scandals such as 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), Tabung Haji (TH), and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) from recurring,” the statement read.
The MACC stated that the government’s decision to strengthen governance and transparency in public financial management by reinvesting all loan repayment collections proves the government’s awareness of ensuring these funds reach the intended target groups without being misappropriated.
“The government’s decision to disclose project information, including contractors and contract values following the Government Procurement Act which will take effect next year, also reflects the government’s transparency in sharing information with the public,” according to the statement.
Meanwhile, the MACC supports the government’s initiative to study the establishment of the Law Reform Commission of Malaysia to identify outdated laws and existing legal gaps, in line with the need to update legal policies to close loopholes for crime.
The MACC is confident that with the strong support of the government and the rakyat, efforts to strengthen integrity, improve governance, and combat corruption can be further enhanced for the well-being of the public as a whole. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Health Ministry to expand outsourcing programme to cut waiting times
Article:
IPOH, Oct 11 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will expand the scope of the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme (HSOP) to cover new areas following an increase in its allocation to RM200 million under Budget 2027, which was tabled on Friday.
Deputy Health Director-General (Medical) Datuk Dr Mohd Azman Yacob said the additional allocation would enable the ministry to refer more patients to private hospitals for faster treatment.
“With the allocation increased from RM144 million to RM200 million, we will focus on HSOP, including expanding it to several new areas deemed suitable.
“This initiative has also proven effective in shortening patients’ waiting times at government hospitals, particularly for Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans, which previously took between three and six months,” he said at a press conference after attending the Public-Private Partnership Empowerment Ceremony for the Cataract Surgery Programme between the Malaysian Government and Perak Community Specialist Hospital (PCSH) here yesterday.
On Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, announced an allocation of RM200 million for outsourcing patient treatment to other hospitals as a measure to reduce waiting times, particularly at government hospitals.
Introduced in 2024, HSOP currently benefits patients requiring treatment in nephrology, cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, paediatric cardiology and radiology.
Mohd Azman said HSOP enabled patients to access treatment at private hospitals more quickly, while the charges imposed remained subject to the rates set by government hospitals.
“For example, if the actual cost of treatment at a private hospital is RM3,000, the patient will pay the applicable government hospital rate, while the government covers the remaining cost through HSOP,” he said.
He added that patients were selected for the programme based on assessments by specialists at government hospitals, specifically for cases requiring urgent treatment and diagnostic procedures. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: New immigration quarters planned for Perak, Sabah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — The construction of new quarters at the Langkap Immigration Detention Depot in Perak and Papar, Sabah, under Budget 2027 will improve the welfare and operational readiness of Immigration Department (JIM) personnel in carrying out enforcement duties.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said more conducive residential facilities would not only enhance the well-being of officers and their families, but also help them focus fully on their responsibilities in law enforcement and immigration detainee management.
He said personnel welfare was not merely about providing facilities, but also formed the foundation of an enforcement organisation’s readiness and effectiveness.
“The department views the announcement under Budget 2027 not merely as an increase in physical facilities, but as a responsibility to translate the government’s commitment into improved performance and service delivery.
“In this regard, the department will extend its full cooperation and commitment in coordinating the implementation of the initiatives to ensure that the intended benefits are realised to the fullest,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Zakaria said the Immigration Department also welcomed the announcement on the construction of the Keningau Immigration Office in Sabah, which is expected to strengthen the department’s capacity to provide more systematic, comfortable and efficient services to the local community.
He said infrastructure development was important to ensure a more organised, comfortable and efficient service environment, in line with the public’s needs and expectations for quality public services.
“Both initiatives represent strategic investments in strengthening the organisation’s capacity and capabilities, while giving balanced attention to the well-being of personnel and the need to provide services to the public,” he said.
When tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Armed Forces Family Housing would be built in Skudai, Johor, along with new quarters at the Langkap Immigration Detention Depot in Perak and Papar, Sabah. The projects would benefit nearly 900 personnel at a cost of more than RM500 million. — Bernama

Title: MCMC probes Facebook post suspected of insulting Islam by mocking Quranic verse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into an individual over Facebook content suspected of insulting Islam.
MCMC said the content concerned the use of the word “lighad”, which refers to verse 18 of Surah al-Hashr, in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s Budget 2027 speech on Friday.
“The content allegedly mocked a Quranic verse, causing concern among the public,” it said in a statement yesterday.
MCMC said it had recorded a statement from the individual to assist in the investigation and seized a mobile phone and an eSIM for forensic examination.
The commission said the case was being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 [Act 588], which provides for a maximum fine of RM500,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
MCMC stressed that freedom of expression on social media must be exercised responsibly, with respect for religious sensitivities and the need to preserve harmony in a multiracial and multireligious society. — Bernama

Title: Cops arrest five men after video of alleged armed assault in Petaling Jaya goes viral
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Police have arrested five men, aged between 30 and 40, on suspicion of being involved in an attack on a man using dangerous weapons at a housing area in Petaling Jaya on Friday.
Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said that during the arrests, police also seized a machete and a saw believed to have been used in the incident.
“At 1.03am yesterday (Friday), the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD) received a police report from a local man stating that he had been attacked by several individuals. Police also tracked down a video related to the incident that went viral on social media,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He added that three of the arrested suspects have multiple past records involving criminal and drug offences, while the other two have no recorded criminal history.
“The case is investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for possessing weapons or dangerous objects during a riot. The public is advised not to spread inaccurate information or make any speculations regarding this incident,” he said.
Shamsudin also urged witnesses with information related to the incident to come forward to the nearest police station or contact the Petaling Jaya IPD operations room directly at 03-79662222 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Jais probes viral post alleging Muslim took part in non-Islamic religious ritual
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 11 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) is investigating a viral post concerning an individual believed to be Muslim who allegedly performed rituals of another religion in violation of Islamic law.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said investigations had begun under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, which cover acts of demonstrating worship in ways that contravene Islamic law and bringing Islam into contempt, according to a report by Bernama.
“So far, Jais has not been able to confirm that the act was committed by the individual concerned during the Thaipusam celebration at Batu Caves, Selangor, as claimed in the viral post.
“We also do not rule out the possibility that the post involved superimposed editing or artificial intelligence (AI),” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Shahzihan said Jais would investigate several aspects of the case, including the location of the incident, more thoroughly and urgently.
“This is to establish Jais’ jurisdiction to take further action under the laws in force.
“Matters concerning the Islamic faith of Muslims in Selangor are taken seriously, and every piece of information or complaint will be investigated, with action taken professionally, firmly, swiftly, accurately and fairly,” he said.
Yesterday, the media reported that the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) was taking action with the relevant authorities over the circulation of several video recordings allegedly showing a Muslim individual participating in non-Islamic religious rituals.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was reported as saying that his department had taken note of the recordings, which were also linked to alleged acts of worship and the use of certain mantras.

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia discuss joint action to tackle transboundary haze
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 11 — Indonesia has confirmed that discussions with Malaysia are underway to detail the best form of cooperation to tackle forest and land fires that have triggered transboundary haze.
Indonesian Communications Agency head Syahganda Nainggolan said good relations between the two countries were an important foundation for finding joint solutions, particularly as firefighting operations faced challenges, including natural factors.
“Malaysia’s Foreign Minister and Indonesia’s Foreign Minister are holding detailed discussions to find solutions and jointly address the forest and land fires,” he told the media on Saturday.
Syahganda was responding to a question about Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement on Malaysia’s readiness to assist Indonesia, as well as a proposal to convene a regional meeting of environment ministers to coordinate efforts to tackle transboundary haze.
“The haze situation is indeed worrying. I personally contacted President Prabowo, and he agreed that the necessary measures should be taken,” Anwar said.
Meanwhile, Indonesia’s Forestry Ministry reported on Saturday that 437 high-confidence hotspots had been detected nationwide as of 9 pm on Friday, up from 387 the previous day.
Of the total, 270 hotspots were detected in six priority provinces across Sumatra and Kalimantan, while 61 aircraft had been deployed for firefighting operations, aerial patrols and weather modification. — Bernama

Title: Two women die after car skids into opposite lane, collides with trailer in Terengganu five-vehicle crash
Article:
BANDAR PERMAISURI, Oct 11 — Two women were killed when the Proton Waja car they were travelling in was involved in a five-vehicle collision at Kilometre 48 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu in Kampung Selamat here yesterday afternoon.
The victims were identified as the driver, trader Nur Fauziah Ismail, 38, from Kampung Apek, and front-seat passenger Zawiah Halias, 41, a trader from Kampung Hulu Kekabu.
Setiu District Police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the crash at about 4pm, while the incident is believed to have occurred at 3.45pm.
He said initial investigations showed that the Proton Waja travelling from Kota Bharu towards Kuala Terengganu was believed to have skidded into the opposite lane before colliding with a Mercedes-Benz trailer.
“Following the collision, the trailer also skidded and grazed a Perodua Aruz multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a Perodua Myvi and a UDT lorry travelling from Kota Bharu towards Kuala Terengganu,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said both victims were pronounced dead at the scene and their bodies sent to the Setiu Hospital Forensic Unit.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Zahril Asri urged road users to obey traffic laws and requested witnesses to contact the Setiu District Police Headquarters Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division to assist in investigations. — Bernama

Title: MACC sets up special team to re-examine RM350,000 corruption allegations against its senior officer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has established a special team to review and re-examine corruption allegations amounting to RM350,000 involving one of its senior officers.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the directive to form the special team was issued immediately following recent calls and the resurfacing of the issue online.
“This step is taken to ensure that the MACC’s integrity remains preserved and public confidence in the anti-corruption institution is not compromised,” he said in a statement yesterday.
The MACC said that the issue had previously been investigated in 2018 and the case was closed after no wrongdoing was proven.
“The MACC emphasises that the commission will not compromise in handling any issue that could affect the credibility of this institution. Therefore, the MACC advises all parties not to make any speculations or spread unverified news regarding the issue,” according to the statement.
Malaysian Corruption Watch (MCW) had earlier urged the MACC and the Anti-Corruption Advisory Board (ACAB) to take immediate action regarding allegations of accepting a bribe of approximately RM350,000 linked to a senior MACC officer.
MCW President Jais Abdul Karim was reported as saying that the allegations, which refer to an incident on November 13, 2017, had gone viral on social media since Friday, though no official clarification confirming its investigation status had been provided. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu to operate as usual today, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual today as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the three states remain under control.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Education Ministry (MOE) will continue to monitor the air quality following the haze currently affecting the country.
“Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual tomorrow (October 11) as the API readings are still under control,” she said in a statement yesterday.
Previously, MOE directed all educational institutions under its purview in areas with API readings exceeding 180 to close starting October 9, while those in areas recording readings above 150 for three consecutive days are to close from October 12.
The closures are to protect the health and safety of students and educators from the haze.
Meanwhile, the MOE has directed State Education Directors (PPN) to set up a Haze Monitoring Task Force Committee to determine daily school operations based on Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
In a statement yesterday, MOE said the committee, comprising State Education Departments (JPN) and District Education Offices (PPD), will monitor API readings at scheduled times daily.
“Based on data from this committee, PPN will decide whether schools operate as usual or switch to Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPr),” the statement said.
Announcements on school status will be made before 2.45 pm on Saturdays for Group A schools and Sundays for Group B schools. On other days, announcements will be issued before 5.45 pm based on API data from the Department of Environment (DOE).
MOE noted that the fixed announcement schedule aims to facilitate travel arrangements for hostel students.
It also advised parents and guardians to stay attentive to official announcements issued through respective JPN, PPD and school communication channels. — Bernama

Title: Johor extends school closures until Oct 16 as haze worsens
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 11 — The Johor government has decided to extend the closure of all schools and educational institutions in the state for five days, from October 12 to 16, due to the haze.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made upon the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, following the worsening air quality.
Muhammad Naqib said the decision also took into account several key factors based on an assessment of the current situation, including projected wind movements from Kalimantan, Indonesia, between October 13 and 15, which could bring transboundary air pollution and affect air quality in the state.
“In addition, the concentration of air pollutants and static atmospheric conditions could cause the haze to persist for a longer period, while Air Pollutant Index (API) readings have been reported at between 170 and 180,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said risk assessments and health statistics regarding the impact of air pollution had also been reviewed, specifically focusing on the risk of respiratory problems among children, students and educators, who are more vulnerable to the effects of haze.
He said that for schools scheduled to conduct academic assessments or evaluations during this period, all related activities would be postponed and rescheduled in accordance with the directives of the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the relevant authorities.
“At the same time, Home-based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) will continue where appropriate to ensure the continuity of the pupils’ learning process,” he added. — Bernama

Title: RM10,000 duty-free shopping coming to Langkawi and Labuan: What can you buy?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The government announced on Friday that the duty-free shopping limit for visitors and tourists in Langkawi and Labuan will be increased to RM10,000 in a move aimed at boosting tourism on the two islands.
However, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027, said visitors and tourists must stay for at least 48 hours to qualify for the higher duty-free allowance.
With the duty-free shopping allowance set to increase to RM10,000, what can visitors actually buy in Langkawi and Labuan?
While both islands offer a wide range of duty-free goods, shoppers hoping to make the most of the higher allowance may want to focus on items that usually cost more on the mainland.
It remains unclear when the new limit will take effect and which product categories will qualify. The availability of specific brands may also vary between retailers and the two islands.
Currently, duty-free allowances for goods purchased on the two islands vary according to the category of items.
Under existing rules, different limits apply to goods such as clothing, cosmetics, food products and alcoholic beverages.
Shoppers who exceed the prescribed limits are generally required to pay duty on the excess amount rather than the entire purchase, subject to the applicable customs rules.
Meanwhile, cigarettes and tobacco products have been subject to tax on all Malaysian duty-free islands, including Langkawi, Labuan, Tioman and Pangkor, since January 1, 2021. This means shoppers no longer enjoy duty-free savings on these products.
Alcoholic beverages, including wine, spirits and malt liquor, remain eligible for duty-free concessions, subject to the applicable conditions. However, the existing allowance is capped at a combined total of one litre per person.
With that in mind, here are some items and brands visitors can look out for:
1. Fashion and accessories
Shoppers can browse branded watches, wallets, leather goods, sportswear, clothing and other accessories.
Brands to look out for may include Casio, G-Shock, Seiko, Citizen, Adidas, Nike and Puma.
2. Perfumes and cosmetics
Branded perfumes, fragrances, skincare products, makeup and beauty gift sets are among the items shoppers can consider.
Brands to look out for include Chanel, Dior, Gucci, Yves Saint Laurent, Calvin Klein, Estée Lauder, Clinique, Shiseido and MAC Cosmetics.
3. Electronics and gadgets
Selected electronic goods, headphones, portable speakers, cameras, personal-care appliances and other gadgets are also worth browsing.
Brands shoppers may find include Sony, JBL, Bose, Apple, Samsung, Philips and Panasonic.
4. Cookware and cutlery
Pots, pans, cups, plates, dinnerware, glassware, casserole dishes and cutlery are among the kitchen essentials shoppers can look for.
Brands to look out for include Corelle, Luminarc, CorningWare, Visions, Pyrex, Arcopal, La Gourmet, Tefal, Joseph Joseph and HappyCall.
5. Bags and suitcases
Travel bags, luggage, suitcases, backpacks, handbags and shoulder bags are other options for shoppers.
Brands to look out for include Samsonite and American Tourister.
6. Chocolates and confectionery
Imported chocolates, sweets, biscuits, cookies and confectionery gift boxes remain popular choices among visitors.
Brands shoppers may find include Ferrero Rocher, Lindt, Toblerone, Godiva, Cadbury, Hershey's and KitKat.
7. Local products and souvenirs
Visitors can also browse locally made chocolates, traditional snacks, batik, handicrafts, textiles, decorative gifts and souvenirs featuring local landmarks.
Malaysian-made food products and locally produced gifts are other options for those looking to bring home something from the islands.

Title: Malaysia has spent decades digitising public healthcare. Why are paper records still in use?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — For a patient visiting a hospital where electronic medical records are already in use, much of the paperwork that has traditionally accompanied a trip to a government hospital can now happen behind a screen.
Registration is recorded electronically, appointments are managed through the hospital’s information system, and doctors can retrieve a patient’s medical information without having to wait for a physical folder to arrive from another department.
The idea behind an electronic medical record (EMR) is straightforward: instead of a patient’s medical history being stored primarily in paper files, the information is recorded and managed digitally, allowing authorised healthcare personnel to retrieve it when needed.
But Malaysia is still in the process of making that transition across its public healthcare system.
For patients who continue to encounter paper-based processes, the contrast between the two systems can sometimes be stark.
Jensen Lim, 38, recalled how his paper appointment book was once drenched in water, creating problems when he needed to arrange his next appointment.
“If you forget to bring the appointment book, you can’t get an appointment or even change the date of an existing appointment.
“Even a surgery appointment was dependent on a cardboard appointment slip,” Lim said when contacted by
Malay Mail
.
At an orthopaedic department, another patient who had suffered a dislocated and fractured shoulder said she was made to wait about two hours while a nurse searched for her medical file.
CK Tan, 70, said the hospital was eventually unable to locate it.
“I cannot comprehend how they lost such a thick file (about one inch).
“The doctor had to retrace my recovery process and what treatments I had undergone leading up to the present follow-up in order to plan for my next rehabilitation steps,” Tan told
Malay Mail
.
A handwritten appointment card from Hospital Kuala Lumpur shows follow-up dates recorded manually, underscoring the continued role of paper records in parts of the public healthcare system. — Picture by Soo Wern Jun
At an oncology department in northern Malaysia, another patient had a similar experience.
Her medical report containing biopsy results went missing, leaving her facing the possibility of having to undergo another procedure.
The file was eventually located several days later after efforts were made to find it.
“I was told that they misplaced my files, which I felt was appalling, given that it was not just a simple cough or flu illness I had,” said Medaline Chong, 60, who was diagnosed with leukaemia.
The inconvenience is not limited to hospital records.
At a dental clinic, Rahimah Mohd Razman, 35, said registration still involves dropping a paper appointment card into a designated box to join the queue.
Patients are now required to make appointments through the MySejahtera mobile application.
While this may sound more efficient, Rahimah said she was unable to choose the clinic where her dental records were kept because there were no appointments available there in the near term.
“I was in too much pain, and the next available slot for that particular clinic was in two months’ time.
“So I resorted to whichever clinic had the closest available slot.
“Because they had no access to my dental records, I had to rely on a photo I took of my tooth’s X-ray for the dentist to understand my case (a follow-up treatment),” Rahimah said.
These are individual experiences and do not suggest that every government hospital or clinic operates this way.
But they illustrate the practical problem EMR is intended to address: ensuring that a patient’s medical information can be retrieved when and where it is needed, without depending on the movement and storage of physical files.
What exactly is an EMR?
An EMR is more than a scanned copy of a paper file.
Currently, the Health Ministry’s hospital information system, HIS@KKM, covers areas including registration, appointments, admissions and medical-record management, as well as clinical documentation across different disciplines.
Other systems support specific areas of care, such as laboratory, pharmacy and radiology services.
This matters because Malaysia’s digital healthcare infrastructure was not built as a single nationwide database.
Different systems were introduced at different times and for different parts of the healthcare system.
Why are hospitals still using paper files?
While electronic records have existed in parts of the public healthcare system for years, not all facilities use the same system, and not all systems are connected.
For example, TPC-OHCIS uses a centralised database and allows records to be accessed by participating facilities using the system. It can also integrate with laboratory, pharmacy and radiology systems, as well as MyHIX, the Malaysian Health Information Exchange.
Hospital systems, meanwhile, have developed along a separate track, with HIS@KKM and specialist systems such as the Radiology Information System (RIS) and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) being expanded at different facilities.
Introducing digital systems does not necessarily mean that every document generated during a patient’s treatment immediately becomes electronic.
Hospital Cyberjaya, for example, operates HIS@KKM, but according to the Selangor Health Department, some medical-record documents still remain outside the system and continue to be managed in physical form.
That reflects a wider challenge: a hospital can have a digital core while some documents, older records or other systems remain outside it.
Paper appointment cards and clinic documents from Hospital Kuala Lumpur, where patients may still need to keep physical records for appointments and follow-up care. — Picture by Soo Wern Jun
What is the government doing now?
The latest push is backed by an additional RM350 million, bringing the allocation for public healthcare digitalisation to RM1 billion.
The wider initiative involves 150 hospitals and 2,000 health clinics nationwide, and includes accelerating EMR implementation and improving internet connectivity at public healthcare facilities.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the additional allocation would allow the ministry to speed up EMR implementation and expand the use of digital medical systems.
He said the initiative was expected to improve efficiency, reduce waiting times, improve the patient experience and ease congestion at healthcare facilities.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said 15 government hospitals were among the initial group expected to benefit, while efforts would be made to increase the number of hospitals and clinics covered.
How Malaysia ended up with multiple digital systems
Malaysia’s move towards digital public healthcare has been more than two decades in the making.
The broader Hospital Information System (HIS) programme was developed in 2002, with modules covering areas including electronic medical records and clinical documentation, patient management, radiology, laboratory, pharmacy and critical care.
Primary healthcare followed a different path.
The Teleprimary Care (TPC) system was introduced in 2005, while the Oral Health Clinical Information System (OHCIS) dates to 2009.
The two were later integrated into TPC-OHCIS, which was piloted in Seremban in 2017.
The Health Ministry describes TPC-OHCIS as an electronic medical record system used at participating primary healthcare facilities, with a centralised database that allows records to be accessed across facilities using the system.
According to the ministry’s 2011 annual report, development of HIS@KKM was about 90 per cent complete that year, with full development then expected by July 2012 before implementation at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun in Ipoh.
In November 2025, the Health Ministry said it was targeting all 150 public hospitals and more than 3,000 primary healthcare facilities nationwide to be equipped with EMR systems by 2029.
Health Ministry’s EMR timeline
The broader effort is intended to support a more connected health-record system, an aspiration the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission described in August 2026 as “One Individual, One Record”.
The result is a healthcare system in which digital tools are already widely used in some settings, but have been introduced at different times and for different purposes.
The challenge now is not simply to add more digital systems, but to ensure they can work together across facilities and levels of care.
Can a patient’s medical record follow them?
One of the goals of a national EMR is to establish the basis for a Lifetime Health Record, facilitate follow-up care at a healthcare facility closer or more convenient to the patient, and reduce repeated laboratory and radiology investigations.
In simple terms, the aim is for the medical record to follow the patient, rather than the patient having to follow the physical record.
What changes for patients?
As the systems become more connected, some changes could be relatively simple from a patient’s perspective.
Patients may no longer have to depend on carrying a physical appointment book, while a doctor at a participating facility could potentially retrieve relevant information from previous treatment instead of waiting for a physical file.
But the bigger change is not simply getting rid of paper.
Malaysia has spent more than two decades building different pieces of a digital healthcare system.
The next stage is making those pieces work together.

Title: Unauthorised oil blending could tarnish Malaysia’s global image, experts warn
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Oil blending activities must obtain written approval from the Customs director-general where required under the relevant regulations, and be backed by complete documentation to ensure legal compliance and transparent transactions, an expert said.
Maritime, Customs and cross-border trade policy and law expert Madzli Harun said every activity involving the import, storage, blending and re-export of oil must be carried out within the scope of the licence and the conditions set by the authorities.
He said blending could alter a product’s composition and specifications, so clear records were needed to verify quantities, cargo movements and the condition of the product before and after the process.
Related documents such as contracts, bills of lading and cargo manifests must be aligned to ensure the information declared matched the actual transactions and the condition of the goods, he said.
“If a premises is only approved for storage, any additional activities such as blending or changing a product’s grade must be scrutinised based on the scope of the licence and the regulations in force.
“Operators must ensure written approval is obtained when required, and that all activities are recorded accurately,” he said at a forum titled “Strengthening Malaysia’s Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia’s Regulatory Landscape”, organised by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd in collaboration with Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).
Madzli said incomplete documentation, or discrepancies between records and the actual condition of the cargo, could raise questions over the declaration of goods, regulatory compliance and tax treatment.
A thorough audit was also important to ensure the volumes of oil received, stored, blended and exported could be identified and matched against the relevant documents, he added.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.
In cross-border trade, he said, determining the origin of goods and their eligibility for treatment under free trade agreements must be based on the rules of origin and the relevant supporting documents.
As such, industry operators must ensure every transaction complied with the set conditions, while the authorities must have sufficient records to assess compliance levels and tax implications, he said.
He said clear controls over blending, including approval requirements and proper documentation, were key to preserving the integrity of the Customs system and reducing the risk of disputes between industry players and the authorities.
Meanwhile, maritime industry expert Nazery Khalid said oil blending carried out without approval, monitoring, compliance with standards and proper documentation must be taken seriously, as incidents could threaten health and safety and undermine the integrity of the authorities responsible for monitoring such activities.
He said if such incidents occurred, questions would arise over compliance with safety procedures, the effectiveness of monitoring and the enforcement of regulations on oil blending.
Approval, documentation oversight and compliance with operating conditions must be given close attention to ensure every activity was carried out in a controlled manner, in line with the set regulations as well as international standards and best practices, he said.
He said weaknesses and a lack of integrity in documentation, supervision and enforcement could not only pose risks to the public and the environment, but also erode the confidence of industry players, trading partners and the international community in the transparency of Malaysia’s cargo-handling regulatory system.
“Inconsistent and inaccurate cargo documents such as the bill of lading and manifest should not be taken lightly, especially for liquid cargo such as petroleum products and palm oil. They could open the door to various forms of misconduct that could harm health and the environment.
“If this situation is not addressed promptly and comprehensively, it could undermine public confidence in the integrity of the industry concerned and damage the country’s image on the international stage,” he said.
At the end of the session, Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.

Title: Better roads, stronger pitch: MB sees Budget 2027 lifting Negeri Sembilan’s investment appeal
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 10 — The provision of better infrastructure facilities is expected to enhance Negeri Sembilan’s attractiveness as an investment destination, in line with the ongoing development of Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0).
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the construction of a new road from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Bandar Enstek was among the key infrastructure facilities that would support development in the area, while facilitating movement and improving accessibility.
“Alhamdulillah, Negeri Sembilan is not being left behind in benefiting from Budget 2027 announced yesterday. Among the initiatives are a new road from KLIA to Bandar Enstek, as well as the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak. The new road will also complement the development of MVV 2.0.
“This is significant and a good selling point for the state government, while giving Negeri Sembilan an advantage in attracting more investors,” he told reporters after the close of the Negeri Sembilan Malaysia Property Expo (Mapex) today, which was also attended by state Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) chairman Datuk Hoo Kim See.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027, said the Madani government would complete the development of MVV 2.0 with infrastructure projects including the new KLIA-Bandar Enstek road, the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak and the implementation of the Klang Valley Dual Track 2 project.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the construction of the Rembau Integrated Health Complex would also benefit the state by expanding healthcare facilities for the public, particularly as several existing hospitals in Negeri Sembilan were facing problems, including a shortage of beds.
He said the facility was important to increase the state’s healthcare service capacity and complement the government’s efforts to improve healthcare facilities to meet the needs of a growing population.
He also expressed hope that initiatives announced under Budget 2027 would be implemented according to schedule to ensure the people could enjoy the intended benefits as planned.
Ismail said smooth implementation within the stipulated timeframe was crucial, as delays or problems with project execution could prompt complaints from the public, who had high expectations following the government’s announcements.
“What matters is not just the announcement of expenditure, but also how it is implemented. Sometimes, we announce a lot, but implementation gets held up and does not proceed on time. This will create problems for the people who have placed their hopes in these announcements,” he said.
He said the state government would continue to facilitate and cooperate through the relevant departments to ensure the projects could be implemented smoothly, allowing the people to benefit within the stipulated timeframe. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Budget 2027 will balance fiscal discipline with cost-of-living relief
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — The government will continue to focus on prudent fiscal management in Budget 2027 to return benefits to the people and reduce cost-of-living pressures, especially for low-income households, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister said that savings from improved governance and efforts to curb leakages will be redirected to the people, in line with the need to strengthen the country’s financial position without compromising assistance to those in need.
Anwar, also the finance minister, said although Malaysia’s inflation rate is around two per cent, one of the lowest in the world, the public still feels cost-of-living pressures due to rising prices of goods and certain services.
“When people ask why this could not be done two years ago, we had to resolve several issues first. We had to address debt, be prudent, and set priorities,” he said in a special Madani Budget 2027 interview aired by RTM tonight.
Anwar noted that the government must balance the need to reduce debt and curb spending with the requirement to increase allocations for critical sectors such as defence, housing for service members and police, and school facilities.
According to him, this approach is important to ensure every ringgit the government spends delivers greater economic and social value for the people.
Anwar said the government’s fiscal space has improved through more disciplined financial management, but these savings must be safeguarded from erosion by leakages and waste.
He noted that a stronger fiscal position enables the government to provide assistance such as sports shoes for schoolchildren, as well as allowances and minimum income support for rubber smallholders and paddy farmers.
“This can all be achieved if we manage finances well and ensure that government expenditure truly reaches the targeted groups,” he stressed.
The prime minister said the government’s economic strategy also focuses on investments in high-value sectors such as information technology and artificial intelligence (AI), but these developments must be accompanied by measures to boost people’s income and productivity.
“Investments, IT, and AI are the things (referencing Budget 2027’s theme) we are ‘reaching for in the skies while anchored on our values’, meaning looking at issues like salaries, the price of goods, the needs of people with disabilities, and children who do not have access to basic facilities,” he said.
Anwar said solid economic growth must translate into quality job opportunities, higher wages, and reduced income inequality, and should not be measured solely by the gross domestic product growth rate.
He said the government would also continue to take into account the needs of social and cultural development in economic planning, including Islamic education training and aid to non-Muslim communities to maintain places of worship.
He acknowledged that Budget 2027 cannot solve all economic problems, but emphasised that the government’s fiscal policy would prioritise easing the burdens on the groups most affected by financial pressures.
In addition, Anwar explained that external factors and global markets influence part of the price of goods, for example, the cost of imported phosphate fertiliser via the Hormuz Strait following the crisis in West Asia.
According to him, fluctuations in commodity prices, logistics costs, and disruptions in international supply chains can directly impact domestic prices, limiting the government’s ability to control all prices.
Nevertheless, he said the government can still reduce price pressures by streamlining the supply chain, expanding farmers’ markets, and increasing sales of goods through the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority.
Therefore, Anwar said the government would provide assistance and facilities based on the country’s financial capacity, with a more targeted approach to ensure public resources are not wasted.
As an example, he cited the decision to maintain subsidised RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre, even as global oil prices rise, as a measure to protect household disposable income.
He said the oil price used in the government’s initial projections was US$70 per barrel, but it rose to about US$110 per barrel, while RON95 petrol remained at RM1.99 per litre.
The decision, he said, reflects the government’s need to balance fiscal pressures from subsidies with the need to maintain stable transportation costs and the public’s purchasing power.
“Ultimately, in managing the national economy, the income and livelihoods of ordinary people become the measuring standards,” he said.
Anwar also emphasised that the government would continue to implement policies based on the country’s fiscal capacity, focusing on strengthening the economy, boosting productivity, reducing leakages, and protecting those most affected by cost-of-living pressures.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled Budget 2027 with the theme “Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values,” with government allocations amounting to RM459.8 billion, plus RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs); RM11 billion in public-private investments; and RM14.2 billion in investments by Federal Statutory Bodies and the Minister of Finance (Incorporated), resulting in Budget 2027 as an expansionary fiscal policy of RM510 billion.
The Fifth Madani Budget aims to translate resilient economic growth into tangible benefits for the people through higher wages, more efficient targeted support, stronger fiscal discipline, and aggressive steps toward higher-value industries. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says reduced waste and leakages created room for more Budget 2027 aid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Budget 2027 is the result of good national financial management, with the savings achieved now being returned to the people rather than enjoyed only by certain groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had to resolve the country’s financial priorities first before gaining a greater capacity to channel savings to the people.
“That is why people ask me, why couldn’t this be done two years ago? We resolved issues according to priority, fixing what is most important first.
“Money must be saved; do not be wasteful, do not lose it, and do not allow leakages... now that it has accumulated, we can return it to the people, not to ministers’ allowances,” he said in the Madani Budget 2027 Special Interview here today.
Anwar said good governance practices allowed the government to provide various forms of assistance and initiatives to the people, including the provision of sports shoes and aid for rubber smallholders and padi farmers.
He said this approach is the foundation for strengthening governance, which allows welfare initiatives to be implemented in stages according to the country’s financial capacity.
The prime minister said the government previously had to focus on debt management and urgent needs, including school facilities and housing for military and police personnel.
He said the savings achieved have now given the government some extra room to increase assistance for the people, but the effort must be accompanied by continuous financial discipline.
“And now, I say, we have a little more capacity. But on the condition that we do not allow leakages to recur,” he added.
When tabling Budget 2027 yesterday, Anwar announced increased allocations for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistances to RM16 billion from RM15 billion, with all STR recipients receiving up to RM150 a month or RM1,800 a year.
Additionally, Malaysians aged 18 and above who do not receive the STR will receive the Madani SARA of RM100 twice, namely before Aidilfitri and in conjunction with the country’s 70th National Day.
The prime minister said both initiatives will benefit up to nine million STR recipients and 13 million Malaysians, including the middle-income group (M40).
The Early Schooling Aid has also been increased to RM200 from RM150 this year, with an RM1 billion allocation benefiting 5.3 million students.
The government will also channel a one-off special financial assistance of RM1,000 to 38,000 taxi and rental car drivers, as well as 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide, following the revenue generated from the sale of ‘H’ special registration plates.
The assistance will be disbursed next week as part of measures to return the revenue to the people. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 more than numbers, says Anwar — it is a promise to the people
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that Budget 2027 is a covenant between the country and its leadership and the people, which must be implemented with full trust and integrity.
The finance minister said the Fifth Madani Budget, formulated by a large team under the Ministry of Finance and other ministries, took into account the needs of various segments of society, ranging from driving economic growth to addressing issues concerning employment, wages and minimum income
“We want to remind all Malaysians from various walks of life that this budget is not merely about managing finances, but must be an agreement bound by a covenant.
“This means a promise, pledge or oath between the country, its leadership and the people. So, we listened to hundreds, and perhaps even more, views from various groups,” he said in the Special Madani Budget 2027 Interview aired by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) tonight.
Anwar said the Madani government under his leadership had always considered all levels of society when formulating Budget 2027, themed “Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values”, while seeking to uphold the dignity and well-being of the people.
The prime minister added that whatever plans implemented by the government under Budget 2027 would ultimately ensure a better quality of life for various segments of society in the future, while taking into account all the challenges faced by the people.
He said Budget 2027 not only focused on major matters such as driving high economic growth, but also extended to issues such as cat welfare, as well as the welfare of gig workers and minimum income.
“The economy may be thriving, but the people may still be burdened. So, this is what I call a philosophy, an approach that takes a more holistic view, and that is essentially what a budget is.
“We have heard about the problems faced by gig workers, e-hailing and p-hailing workers. These are things that did not exist 10 years ago. They are new issues,” he said.
Anwar also explained that Budget 2027 was the result of how the country was being managed well, with the highest leadership always upholding its trust and responsibility.
“This is a budget where the country upholds its trust, safeguards it as a trust, and treats it as a covenant. It is a promise that must be fulfilled in earnest,” he said.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, allocating RM510 billion to uphold the dignity and well-being of the people at all levels.
Budget 2027 outlines eight key pillars, encompassing commitments ranging from improving the people’s quality of life to strengthening the country’s resilience and future.
When tabling the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, Anwar summed up the commitment as the “National Covenant” — a pledge that the country’s progress would ultimately translate into a more dignified life for the people and strengthen Malaysia for future generations. — Bernama

Title: Grieving mother haunted by memories of her three children killed in Pontian accident
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The mother of the three siblings who tragically died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong here, admits that she still finds it difficult to look at her children’s clothes and school bags as they serve as painful reminders of them.
Julaiha Munaji, 44, said the simultaneous loss of Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha Norlizan, 8, is the heaviest trial she and her family have ever faced.
She shared that the loss of her youngest child, Puteri Naufa, is felt the most because the only daughter among her six children was exceptionally close to her.
“I have six children, five boys and one girl. For years, my husband and I prayed for a daughter, but I was only blessed to have her with me for eight years.
“Even though I lost her two days ago, I accept it with a quiet heart and am grateful for the chance to raise her, even if it was only for a short time,” she told Bernama when met at her home in Kampung Parit Haji Siraj today.
Julaiha said among the things she misses the most is her daily routine of preparing breakfast and packed meals for her children before starting the day.
She added that she can still vividly picture the playful antics of her three children in the yard every evening, memories that are hard to forget.
“It will probably take time for me to get used to this loss. Losing even one child is heavy enough, but losing three all at once is unbearable,” she said.
Last Thursday, the three siblings died after the motorcycle they were riding collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat, Kayu Ara Pasong at around 7:20 am, just after returning from Sekolah Kebangsaan Parit Sapran.
At the time, Nor Daniel Aiman was on his way back after taking his two younger siblings to the school to inform them that classes were canceled due to deteriorating air quality caused by haze.
Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Moin Hussain reported that two of the pillion riders died at the scene, while the motorcycle rider passed away while on the way to Pontian Hospital.
All schools in Johor were closed last Thursday and Friday due to the declining air quality, affecting more than 1,000 schools and approximately 600,000 students. — Bernama

Title: Melaka tourist spots remain busy despite unhealthy API readings
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 10 — Tourist spots around Banda Hilir here continue to draw local and foreign visitors despite Melaka recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings since Thursday due to the haze.
A Bernama check at the Stadthuys and Jonker Walk found that tourists were still visiting the popular attractions, while souvenir and handicraft shops remained open as usual.
However, few tourists and traders were seen wearing face masks to protect themselves from the effects of unhealthy air quality.
Asmah Zulkifli, 66, from Kuala Lumpur, said the haze had not deterred her and several friends from visiting tourist attractions, including the Stadthuys, after attending a friend’s wedding reception in Bukit Katil here.
“If not for the wedding, we wouldn’t have come to Melaka. Since we are here, we decided to drop by Banda Hilir.
“Alhamdulillah, even though it is hazy, this area is still attracting many visitors and remains lively,” said the former civil servant, who will return to Kuala Lumpur tomorrow afternoon.
She said they planned to visit several other tourist attractions if the haze did not reach hazardous levels.
Trishaw peddler Muhammad Azhan Fikry Munawir, 28, said tourism activities in the area remained lively, with local and foreign tour groups continuing to visit.
“Perhaps, to the public, the impact of the haze is not like COVID. Besides, tourist areas in Melaka are still operating as usual.
“It is just that trishaw peddlers have to be more careful because we spend longer periods outdoors and are more exposed to the health effects,” said Muhammad Azhan, who has worked as a trishaw peddler for 10 years.
Meanwhile, souvenir trader Amalina Zulkifli, 34, said the haze had not deterred tourists from visiting the UNESCO World Heritage Site.
“Alhamdulillah, there are many tourists around this area today. Only yesterday there were slightly fewer, perhaps because it was a working day and the API reading was higher than today,” she said.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed that API readings in Melaka had declined compared with yesterday but remained in the unhealthy range as of 5 pm today, with Alor Gajah and Bandaraya Melaka each recording 164, while Bukit Rambai recorded 163. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid wants tahfiz graduates equipped for careers in technology, engineering and medicine
Article:
BANGI, Oct 10 — Tahfiz graduates should have wider opportunities to pursue higher education and professional careers in fields such as technology, engineering and medicine to meet the country’s evolving workforce needs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said tahfiz education should go beyond Quran memorisation by equipping graduates with the knowledge, skills and qualifications needed to pursue a broader range of careers.
“My principle is simple. Tahfiz graduates should not have to choose between religion and their ambitions. They should be given the opportunity to deepen their religious knowledge while acquiring the skills and qualifications needed for professional careers,” he said at the 10th Huffaz Nusantara Permata Al-Quran Convocation at the German-Malaysian Institute here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who chairs the National Tahfiz Council, said advances in artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and high technology made it increasingly important for tahfiz graduates to develop skills that would enable them to compete across various sectors.
As such, he said tahfiz education must also keep pace with the country’s human capital needs by providing more pathways to universities, technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions, industry and professional fields.
Achieving this would require cooperation among the government, tahfiz institutions, universities and industry to ensure graduates had clear opportunities to progress after completing their studies.
“Tahfiz graduates must not be left to find their own way after graduation. The ecosystem must help them move on to the next stage,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts to strengthen tahfiz education included enhancing the National Tahfiz Education Policy, developing the Malaysian Tahfiz Recognition Standard and strengthening pathways through the Malaysian Tahfiz Certificate to broaden graduates’ education and career options.
He also welcomed the increased allocation for Islamic affairs, pondok schools, tahfiz institutions and people’s religious schools under Budget 2027, as well as improved allowances for religious teachers and mosque personnel
“This reflects the government’s commitment to supporting those involved in Islamic religious affairs, and is a positive development that deserves the support of all parties,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, announced that the allocation for Islamic affairs had been increased to RM3.1 billion from RM2.6 billion this year. — Bernama

Title: Lights on: Works Department to extend streetlight operating hours during haze
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The Public Works Department (JKR) will extend the operating hours of its streetlights by up to two hours during haze conditions to help improve visibility for road users.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the measure, implemented through JKR’s Electrical Engineering Branch, was prompted by haze conditions that had reduced visibility and increased the risk of accidents.
He said streetlights using timer systems currently typically operated from 7 pm to 7 am.
“Each streetlight has a timer setting that can be adjusted. During haze conditions, the operating hours can be extended by up to two hours.
“We will also refer the matter to local authorities, such as municipal councils and city halls, to encourage them to take similar measures,” he told reporters after visiting the family of three siblings who died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj here today.
The three siblings, aged eight to 18, were killed on Thursday after the motorcycle they were on collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat in Kayu Ara Pason amid hazy weather and limited visibility.
Ahmad also advised road users to exercise greater caution and ensure safe visibility when driving in hazy conditions. — Bernama

Title: Air quality acceptable for now, Kedah schools to open as usual tomorrow
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 10 — All educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring areas in the state were recorded below 100 as of 2 pm today.
The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this was, however, subject to any further directives from the Ministry of Education and the relevant authorities.
“The Kedah JPN expresses its appreciation for the concern and decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, regarding the importance of safeguarding the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel following the haze affecting several areas in the country.
“The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual,” the statement said.
The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.
“Schools should also pay close attention to students and education personnel experiencing health problems, particularly those who are sensitive to air quality conditions, and take appropriate action if any students or education personnel show signs of ill health.
“The Kedah JPN will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and coordinate action with all District Education Offices and educational institutions based on the latest readings and directives from the authorities,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to prioritise mental health in World Mental Health Day post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 —The public should prioritise their mental health and not hesitate to seek help when experiencing stress or feeling overburdened by the demands of daily life, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said mental health should be cared for alongside physical health, particularly when dealing with the demands of work, family and everyday life.
“In the midst of busy work, family and daily life, do not forget to look after our mental health just as we look after our physical health,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with World Mental Health Day today.
Fahmi said those who felt overwhelmed, exhausted or struggled to cope on their own should talk to someone they trusted and seek help if necessary.
He also reminded the public that taking a break and giving themselves some space was nothing to feel guilty about.
World Mental Health Day is observed on October 10 every year to raise public awareness of the importance of mental health worldwide. — Bernama

Title: President El-Sisi invites Malaysia’s King, PM to visit Egypt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt.
The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today.
“It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today. — Bernama

Title: Egypt president El-Sisi praises Malaysia for helping injured Gazans, backs Palestinian state
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has reaffirmed Egypt’s support for a two-state solution to the Palestinian issue, with an independent Palestinian state based on the July 4, 1967 borders and East Jerusalem as its capital.
He said the Palestinian issue remained central to West Asia and was among the key matters discussed during his meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“We stressed together (during the meeting) the necessity for a just and comprehensive settlement according to the international resolutions, and the two-state solution to ensure a Palestinian independent state is established,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar in Putrajaya today.
El-Sisi also commended Malaysia’s support for the Palestinian people, particularly its humanitarian assistance and efforts to provide medical treatment for injured Palestinians from Gaza.
“I would be remiss if I didn't applaud Malaysia's supporting stance regarding the Palestinian issue and its keenness to provide humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian people and also hosting Palestinian second-injured people to get medical care here in Malaysia,” he said.
On the wider regional situation, El-Sisi said Egypt was making relentless efforts to halt the escalation in West Asia, stressing that collective efforts were necessary to establish peace and uphold international law.
“I would like to seize this opportunity to stress Egypt's relentless efforts to stop the escalation in West Asia,” he said, adding that all parties must work together to establish peace while respecting national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the principle of non-interference in domestic affairs.
“I just want to confirm here that there is a total convergence between myself and the prime minister regarding the issues of the region and the world, that the political and the diplomatic tracks, respecting international law, are the only way to find lasting and permanent solutions to the crisis in the Gulf,” he said.
He also said that both leaders discussed developments in the Horn of Africa and their potential implications for the wider region.
Malaysia and Egypt have maintained diplomatic relations since November 10, 1959, describing their partnership as founded on mutual respect, shared values, and common aspirations.
During El-Sisi’s state visit to Malaysia on October 9 and 10, the two countries elevated their bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership and reaffirmed their commitment to closer cooperation across various sectors.
The two leaders also reaffirmed in a joint statement that Palestine remained the core issue in West Asia, rejecting plans to displace Palestinians and calling for the consolidation of the ceasefire in Gaza, unrestricted humanitarian assistance, and the implementation of relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.
His state visit to Malaysia — his first to the country since assuming office in June 2014 — is at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. El-Sisi is accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia and Egypt eye easier travel, more business as trade surges, says PM
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will focus on expanding trade and investment cooperation, improving flight connectivity and exploring new areas of economic collaboration at a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting, agreed upon by the two countries’ foreign ministers, would provide a platform to translate growing bilateral ties into broader economic opportunities.
He said bilateral trade had increased 74.7 per cent this year, but stressed that the growth came from a low base, leaving considerable room for further expansion.
“We have achieved this phenomenal increase this year, rising to 74.7 per cent of trade, but then it is from a very, very low base,” said the prime minister.
Anwar was speaking at a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in conjunction with the latter’s two-day state visit to Malaysia.
He said Malaysia saw considerable potential to expand cooperation with Egypt in several sectors, including semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.
Malaysia was also looking at emerging economies, including Brics countries, as potential sources of pharmaceutical products, with Egypt among the countries that could meet its needs.
“Egypt has the potential to become a destination for sourcing pharmaceuticals,” said Anwar.
He said improved air connectivity, including more regular flights, would also be important in facilitating trade, investment and tourism between the two countries.
Anwar described Egypt as an important country in the Arab world and Africa, adding that closer engagement would give Malaysia greater opportunities to expand its economic presence in the region.
Earlier, the prime minister and his counterpart held a four-eyed meeting at the Seri Perdana Complex here today, marking a significant step towards elevating Malaysia-Egypt relations to a strategic partnership after more than six decades of diplomatic ties.
The meeting, held in conjunction with El-Sisi’s two-day state visit to Malaysia, provided an opportunity for both leaders to review bilateral cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration and exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.
The Egyptian president, who is undertaking his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, arrived at the complex at 12.58pm for a series of official engagements aimed at strengthening political, economic and diplomatic relations between the two nations.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh-largest trading partner in Africa, with total bilateral trade valued at RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion).
Malaysia’s exports to Egypt amounted to RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion), while imports totalled RM530 million (US$0.12 billion).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade surged 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$0.87 billion). — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry drafting national registry for persons with disabilities to improve service planning
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through its Family Health Development Division’s Persons with Disabilities (PWD) Sector, has initiated strategic discussions on the development of the MOH PWD Strategic Plan.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was also drafting a proposal for a national-level PWD Registry (OKU Registry), which would incorporate data and needs profiles of the cerebral palsy (CP) community.
“This step shows that your voices are being heard and translated into structured action at the ministry level to plan a service delivery system driven by actual data.
“Approaches such as the CP Living Library featured in this symposium are highly significant. Clinical knowledge provides medical and scientific evidence, while your lived experiences offer a human and empathetic perspective,” he said.
He was speaking at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Cerebral Palsy Symposium, organised by Gabungan Anak-Anak Palsi Serebrum (GAPS) at the Shah Alam Convention Centre here today.
MOH records showed that 1,076 children with CP had been registered and received early intervention services at health clinics nationwide from 2016 to 2025.
Speaking to reporters, Dzulkefly said the strategic plan was still at an early stage, but it was important to ensure that the needs of individuals with CP continued to receive attention throughout their lives.
He said CP required not only care during childhood but also continuous support as individuals transitioned into adolescence and adulthood.
“This is a lifelong need. We want to ensure this group has the opportunity to lead lives like everyone else, including in terms of careers, social relationships and starting a family.
“Our challenge is to ensure they are not excluded from the support system after leaving school. They need more than empathy and sympathy; they need an ecosystem that enables them to live a normal, dignified and inclusive life throughout their lives,” he said.
On the expected timeline for developing the PWD Registry, Dzulkefly said the initiative would be implemented continuously through an approach of ongoing improvement.
He said data collection had to begin in an organised and structured manner to ensure the registry contained high-quality data that could support more effective service planning. — Bernama
